```{r}
fmt_tbl <- function(df, right = NULL, caption = NULL) {
  right_cols <- union(names(df)[vapply(df, is.numeric, TRUE)], right)
  left_cols <- setdiff(names(df), right_cols)
  ft <- flextable::flextable(df)
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, size = 9, part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, align = "center", part = "header")
  if (length(right_cols)) ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = right_cols, align = "right", part = "body")
  if (length(left_cols)) ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = left_cols, align = "left", part = "body")
  ft <- flextable::line_spacing(ft, space = 1, part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::padding(ft, padding.top = 1, padding.bottom = 1,part = "all")
  if (!is.null(caption)) ft <- flextable::set_caption(ft, caption)
  flextable::set_table_properties(ft, layout = "autofit", width = 1)
}

in_km <- function(x, km = "+proj=utm +zone=5 +datum=WGS84 +units=km +no_defs") {
  if (!inherits(x, "SpatRaster")) return(sf::st_transform(x, km))
  ext(x) <- as.vector(ext(x)) / 1000
  crs(x) <- km
  x
}

frame_at_scale <- function(x, scale, width_in, height_in, crs = "EPSG:32605") {
  bb <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(x, crs))
  cx <- mean(bb[c("xmin", "xmax")]); cy <- mean(bb[c("ymin", "ymax")])
  hw <- width_in  * 0.0254 * scale / 2
  hh <- height_in * 0.0254 * scale / 2
  sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = cx - hw, ymin = cy - hh, xmax = cx + hw, ymax = cy + hh),
              crs = sf::st_crs(crs))
}

scale_label <- function(scale) paste0("1:", format(scale, big.mark = ",", scientific = F))

map_frame <- function(title, legend=tmap::tm_pos_out("right","center"), ...) {

}
```

# Abstract

```{r}
#| label: abstract-numbers
#| echo: true
#| output: false
change_a <- read.csv("03.outputs/stand_change.csv"); struct_a <- as.matrix(read.csv("03.outputs/landscape_structure.csv", row.names = 1))  # the abstract renders before the chunks that compute its numbers, so it reads the copies they saved
strip_a <- read.csv("03.outputs/statewide_strip.csv"); regions_a <- as.matrix(read.csv("03.outputs/statewide_regions.csv", row.names = 1)); area_a <- read.csv("03.outputs/statewide_area.csv"); fia_a <- as.matrix(read.csv("03.outputs/fia_ground.csv", row.names = 1))
```

Spruce beetle outbreaks have taken the large white spruce of Southcentral Alaska first in every recorded outbreak, and the hazard ratings that forest managers use to find the stands at risk have rested since 1976 on diameter, basal area and spruce share measured on the ground, which no agency can measure across a state. Whether free satellite measures of stand structure rank the stands an outbreak kills had not been tested. This study scored the slope-corrected Sentinel-1 radar level of October 2014 to December 2016, before the outbreak reached the Susitna valley, and three independent canopy height maps against the dead spruce crowns that Zwieback et al. (2024) delineated on a WorldView-2 image of 2 August 2021, on 510 stand cells of 90 m in their training areas and `r format(struct_a["n", "height_eth"], big.mark = ",")` cells of their severity map, then pooled every Sentinel-1 scene over Alaska into a 90 m map of the pre-outbreak level and tested the map against the aerial detection survey in four regions and against `r sum(fia_a["plots", ])` Forest Inventory and Analysis plots. The radar level of the descending orbit ranked the stands the outbreak killed above the living stands with an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", change_a$auc_pre[change_a$band == "VV131"])` on the crown labels, the statewide product `r sprintf("%.2f", strip_a$AUC)` on the severity map and canopy height `r sprintf("%.2f", struct_a["AUC", "height_eth"])`, and the dead stands stood `r sprintf("%.1f", struct_a["dead", "height_eth"] - struct_a["alive", "height_eth"])` m taller before the outbreak. Against the survey the radar map ranked attacked above unattacked forest at `r sprintf("%.2f", regions_a["AUC_VV", "kenai"])` on the Kenai Peninsula and `r sprintf("%.2f", regions_a["AUC_VV", "matsu"])` in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough but not in the Copper River basin (`r sprintf("%.2f", regions_a["AUC_VV", "copper"])`), where the stands are shorter and darker and the height map alone held (`r sprintf("%.2f", regions_a["AUC_height", "copper"])`), and on the ground the dead white spruce were `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_a["ht_dead", "matsu"] - fia_a["ht_live", "matsu"])` m taller than the live trees beside them in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough (p < 0.001) and no taller on the Interior plots measured before the outbreak's northern front arrived. Of the `r format(round(area_a$forest_km2[area_a$region == "alaska"]), big.mark = ",")` km² of forest in Alaska, `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * area_a$susceptible_km2[area_a$region == "alaska"] / area_a$forest_km2[area_a$region == "alaska"])` per cent reached the level at which the validation strip's stands died. The map was drawn with no beetle data and is offered to the managers preparing their stands for the next outbreak.

# Introduction

The spruce beetle, *Dendroctonus rufipennis* (Kirby) (Coleoptera: Curculionidae, Scolytinae), killed spruce across more than 500,000 ha of Alaska at the peak of the 1990s outbreak, about 30 million trees in 1996 alone [@Holsten_2001], and a new outbreak has spread from the Susitna lowlands of Southcentral Alaska since about 2016 [@Zwieback_2024]. The beetle breeds in windthrown spruce and in the lower boles of standing trees, and its preference is for large mature trees, so that "Once the availability of windthrown spruce is exhausted, mature adult spruce beetles often transition to attacking live spruces, which can lead to outbreaks" [@Fettig_2026, p. 1]. The adult flight in Southcentral Alaska began in the first week of June in 1999 and 2000, with attacks on standing trees one to two weeks after the peak of the flight [@Holsten_2001], and most beetles dispersed 90 to 300 m from their overwintering sites, a few as far as 600 m [@Werner_1997]. Forest managers suppress local populations with sanitation harvests, trap trees and pheromones, and the Forest Service has rated stands for hazard since 1976 so that prevention can be directed to the stands most likely to be attacked [@Fettig_2026; @Schmid_1976].

Which trees the beetle takes has been known since the first systematic study of an outbreak. On the White River National Forest of Colorado in the 1940s, @Massey_1954 [p. 13] recorded that the beetle "prefers the large, more mature trees" and moved to smaller diameter classes only as the large trees were used up, 75 per cent of the trees of 36 to 38 inches in diameter being dead by 1943, and the average diameter of infested trees fell from 21 to 17 to 15 inches as that outbreak ran [@Massey_1954; @Schmid_1976]. The same order was recorded in Alaska in every outbreak since. In a white spruce and birch stand near Fairbanks the beetle killed 64.6 per cent of the spruce of 5 inches and more while "Survival of spruce was greater in smaller diameters" [@Baker_1974, p. 423]; in the Resurrection Creek watershed of the Kenai Peninsula, where 29 per cent of the white spruce died between 1976 and 1980, "Mortality was greatest in the larger diameter classes during the early part of the infestation, but smaller diameter trees were subsequently attacked as the number of noninfested trees declined" [@Werner_1983, p. 96]; a 14-year transect through a mixed white spruce stand on the Kenai "confirmed bark beetle preference for attacking large-diameter, slow-growing spruce" [@Holsten_1984, p. 39]; and in the Kennicott valley of the Copper River basin "Mortality increased with increasing DBH and decreasing BAI", survival being higher for younger, smaller and faster-growing trees [@Doak_2004, p. 810]. In Utah the 1990s outbreak removed 78 per cent of the Engelmann spruce basal area of 5 inches and more by 1996 and 90 per cent by 1998 [@Dymerski_2001], in Colorado the 1940s outbreak left stands with reduced average and maximum diameters, heights and ages and released the small spruce the beetle had not attacked [@Veblen_1991], and in central British Columbia the incidence of infestation rose with site quality, stand age and the spruce share of the stand [@Safranyik_1985].

The size preference has a mechanism and a qualification. Attacks on standing trees stop 12 to 15 m above the ground, so the number of beetles a tree absorbs rises with its diameter rather than its height [@Schmid_1977]. The qualification came from the Kenai Peninsula in the early years of the 1970s outbreak, where @Hard_1983 [p. 678] found that "Diameter was not an important criterion for spruce susceptibility to attack or death unless large diameter was coupled with slower than average radial growth in the last 5 years, an apparent indicator of current tree vigor", the per cent mortality of a stand being "directly related to number of spruce per hectare greater than 24.1 cm in diameter" once that growth was accounted for. @Hard_1985 [p. 839] then showed that the attacked and killed trees had grown more slowly than the unattacked trees of the same plots, that the trees killed and the trees that repelled attack "did not differ in diameter", and that larger diameters and faster growth went together in the less heavily stocked stands. The Forest Service synthesis of that work states the rule in a sentence, "Spruce beetles preferentially attack and kill large diameter trees that have been growing slowly at breast height" [@Hard_1985b, p. 7], and the stands least susceptible in the early years of an outbreak were those growing fast at low stocking [@Hard_1985b]. Only beetles from eruptive populations colonise defended healthy trees, so the rule describes an outbreak and not an endemic population [@Wallin_2004], and host species matters in Alaska, where more beetles are produced in white spruce but outbreaks have been more frequent and severe in Lutz spruce [@Holsten_1990].

Hazard ratings carried the rule from the tree to the stand. @Schmid_1976 [p. 1] rated Engelmann spruce stands "on the basis of physiographic location, tree diameter, basal area, and percentage of spruce in the canopy", scoring as high hazard a stand in a well-drained creek bottom with an average diameter above 16 inches, a basal area above 150 square feet per acre and more than 65 per cent spruce. For the Kenai Peninsula, @Reynolds_1994b built a decision tree for Lutz spruce stands on total basal area, the spruce share of basal area, the share of spruce basal area in trees over 25 cm, elevation and aspect, which predicted high hazard correctly for 73 per cent of stands, and found with a panel of experts that stand hazard and windthrown trees together carried almost two thirds of the importance in the risk of an outbreak [@Reynolds_1994]. The current Forest Service leaflet gives the thresholds now in use, stands "with average spruce diameters >15.7 inches (40 cm) DBH, basal areas >148.1 ft2/acre (34 m2/ha), and a live spruce component >60 percent in drainage bottoms" [@Fettig_2026, p. 8]. Every one of these ratings takes its diameter, basal area and spruce share from a cruise, and thinning the large slowly growing trees out of a stand has been the management that follows from them [@Hard_1985b; @Fettig_2007; @Hansen_2010; @Temperli_2014; @Windmuller_Campione_2015]. Stand age and fire history govern the same attributes at the landscape scale, in that young stands after fire escaped the outbreaks of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries in Colorado [@Kulakowski_2006; @Bakaj_2016].

Remote sensing has been turned on the damage rather than on the stands at risk. The aerial detection survey is the operational record of the outbreak in Alaska, and its sketched polygons record what an observer saw in a year and understate dispersed low-severity mortality [@Zwieback_2024]. Landsat change methods map the severe stands, and in Colorado they tracked the progression of a spruce beetle outbreak from calibrated composites and dense time series [@Woodward_2018; @Ye_2021], but @Zwieback_2024 mapped dead spruce at crown scale from 2 m WorldView-2 imagery in the Susitna valley and found that "approximately 90% of dead trees pixels were found in low-severity stands" while "a clear relation between SWIR reflectance change and severity only emerging above 0.1 severity" [@Zwieback_2024, p. 412], so that most of the mortality lay below what Landsat can see. In Alaska, crown-scale detection of beetle status from airborne hyperspectral and lidar data reached "78% accuracy for all three health statuses" and 97 per cent for non-infested against dead crowns [@Cessna_2021], at a cost in data that no state can bear. Radar had scarcely been used for insect damage before Sentinel-1, and the review of @Hollaus_2019 found that shorter wavelengths had shown more potential than L-band; in Bavaria a random forest on Sentinel-1 features explained 83 to 89 per cent of the variance in a vitality score back-dated from deadwood polygons [@Hechtl_2025], measured on pixels split at random within polygons. No study has measured Sentinel-1 or satellite canopy height against spruce beetle mortality at the stand scale on areas held out whole, and no study has mapped the stands susceptible to the spruce beetle across a region from satellite data without a cruise.

What the satellites measure is the same thing the hazard ratings measure. C-band backscatter over forest rises with the height and biomass of the canopy [@Kellndorfer_2022], a global 10 m map of canopy height has been fitted from Sentinel-2 imagery to the heights of the GEDI lidar with an average root mean square error of 7.3 m [@Lang_2023], and L-band backscatter rises with woody biomass [@Shimada_2014]. A map of tall spruce stands is therefore a map of the large dominant trees the beetle takes, with the diameter, basal area and spruce share of the hazard ratings standing behind it (@tbl-attributes). This study used the crown labels and the severity map of @Zwieback_2024 as the ground truth against which to validate that measure, and then mapped it across Alaska, with the following objectives.

1. Validate, against the dead spruce crowns and the severity map of @Zwieback_2024, that the Sentinel-1 radar level before the outbreak and satellite canopy height rank the stands the outbreak killed above the stands it left alive, and establish what the radar level measures.
2. Map the susceptible spruce stands across Alaska from the pre-outbreak Sentinel-1 level and canopy height, and test the map against the aerial detection survey in the Kenai Peninsula, the Matanuska-Susitna Borough and the Copper River basin and at the outbreak's northern front in the Interior, and against the Forest Inventory and Analysis plots of the same regions.

# Study area

```{r}
#| label: areas
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Zwieback et al. (2024) dead spruce crown labels, Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10569990, CC-BY 4.0.
# The list files name the WorldView-2 image each area was delineated on.
lab_dir <- "02.inputs/zwieback-labels"
areas <- rbind(transform(read.csv(file.path(lab_dir, "gpkg/list"), colClasses = "character"), set = "training", dir = "gpkg"),
               transform(read.csv(file.path(lab_dir, "gpkg_validation/list_validation"), colClasses = "character"), set = "test", dir = "gpkg_validation"))
areas$year <- ifelse(areas$image == "014782712010_01", 2021L, 2013L)  # the post-outbreak image of 2021-08-02 and the pre-outbreak image of 2013-07-14
read_area <- function(i) lapply(c(extent = "_extent.gpkg", crowns = "_labels.gpkg"), function(s) sf::st_read(file.path(lab_dir, areas$dir[i], paste0(areas$roi[i], s)), quiet = TRUE))
info <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(areas)), read_area)
areas <- sf::st_sf(areas, crowns = sapply(info, function(a) nrow(a$crowns)), geometry = do.call(c, lapply(info, function(a) sf::st_geometry(a$extent))))
cells_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/tile_cells.csv"
if (!file.exists(cells_csv)) write.csv(do.call(rbind, lapply(which(areas$year == 2021), function(i) {  # dead crown cover of each 10 m cell, on the UTM 5N grid
  a <- info[[i]]; b <- sf::st_bbox(a$extent)
  tpl <- terra::rast(xmin = floor(b$xmin / 10) * 10, xmax = ceiling(b$xmax / 10) * 10, ymin = floor(b$ymin / 10) * 10, ymax = ceiling(b$ymax / 10) * 10, resolution = 10, crs = "EPSG:32605")
  f <- if (nrow(a$crowns)) terra::rasterize(terra::vect(a$crowns), tpl, cover = TRUE) else terra::init(tpl, 0); f[is.na(f)] <- 0
  d <- setNames(as.data.frame(f, xy = TRUE), c("x", "y", "dead"))
  data.frame(roi = areas$roi[i], set = areas$set[i], d[sf::st_intersects(sf::st_as_sf(d, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605), a$extent, sparse = FALSE)[, 1], ])
})), cells_csv, row.names = FALSE)
cells <- read.csv(cells_csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character"))
used <- areas[areas$year == 2021, ]
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-study
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: "Alaska in the Alaska Albers projection (EPSG:3338), with the spruce beetle damage mapped by the aerial detection survey from 2016 to 2024, the four regions in which the statewide map was tested, and the validation strip of the Susitna valley in which Zwieback et al. (2024) mapped dead spruce crowns on a WorldView-2 image of 2 August 2021."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.6
# USFS Forest Health Protection aerial detection survey damage areas, Alaska Region 10, all years.
# https://www.fs.usda.gov/foresthealth/docs/IDS_Data_for_Download/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb.zip
# United States Census Bureau cartographic boundary file of states, 2023, 1:20,000,000.
# https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/GENZ2023/shp/cb_2023_us_state_20m.zip
# US Census TIGER/Line 2018 county boundaries, Earth Engine TIGER/2018/Counties (row `TIGER/2018/Counties` of 02.inputs/README.md).
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/TIGER_2018_Counties
ads_ak <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_read("02.inputs/ids-region10/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb", quiet = TRUE,
                   query = "SELECT SURVEY_YEAR, Shape FROM DAMAGE_AREAS_FLAT_AllYears_AK_Rgn10 WHERE DCA_CODE = 11009 AND SURVEY_YEAR BETWEEN 2016 AND 2024"), 3338)
frame <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(sf::st_buffer(sf::st_convex_hull(sf::st_union(sf::st_transform(used, 3338))), 20000)))  # the label areas and 20 km around them
ads <- sf::st_intersection(ads_ak, frame)
states_zip <- "02.inputs/context/cb_2023_us_state_20m.zip"
if (!file.exists(states_zip)) download.file("https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/GENZ2023/shp/cb_2023_us_state_20m.zip", states_zip, mode = "wb")
alaska <- sf::st_transform(subset(sf::st_read(file.path("/vsizip", states_zip, "cb_2023_us_state_20m.shp"), quiet = TRUE), STUSPS == "AK"), 3338)
regions <- list(kenai = "02122", matsu = "02170", copper = "02261", interior = c("02068", "02090", "02240"))  # the Kenai Peninsula Borough, the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, the Valdez-Cordova census area holding the Copper River basin, and the Denali Borough, Fairbanks North Star Borough and Southeast Fairbanks census area of the Tanana valley
region_names <- c(kenai = "Kenai Peninsula", matsu = "Matanuska-Susitna", copper = "Copper River", interior = "Interior")
regions_geojson <- "02.inputs/context/regions_tiger2018.geojson"
if (!file.exists(regions_geojson)) download.file(ee$FeatureCollection("TIGER/2018/Counties")$filter(ee$Filter$inList("GEOID", as.list(unname(unlist(regions)))))$getDownloadURL("geojson"), regions_geojson, quiet = TRUE)  # unnamed, or reticulate sends a dictionary
cty <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_read(regions_geojson, quiet = TRUE), 3338)
reg_sf <- sf::st_cast(do.call(rbind, lapply(names(regions), function(nm) sf::st_sf(region = nm, geometry = sf::st_union(sf::st_geometry(cty[cty$GEOID %in% regions[[nm]], ]))))), "MULTIPOLYGON")  # one multipolygon per region, so that terra transfers every part
reg_sf$name <- region_names[reg_sf$region]
ggplot() + geom_sf(data = alaska, fill = "grey92", colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.2) + geom_sf(data = ads_ak, fill = "#C0392B", colour = "#C0392B", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = reg_sf, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) + geom_sf(data = frame, fill = NA, colour = "#1F618D", linewidth = 0.7) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(data = reg_sf, aes(label = name, geometry = geometry), stat = "sf_coordinates", size = 2.6, label.size = 0.2, seed = 1, min.segment.length = 0) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-1.55e6, 1.45e6), ylim = c(4.2e5, 2.35e6)) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + th
```

The study covered the forest of Alaska, which the Sentinel-1 constellation imaged from October 2014 (@fig-study). The forest is boreal, white spruce (*Picea glauca* (Moench) Voss) and black spruce (*P. mariana* (Mill.) Britton et al.) with Alaska birch (*Betula neoalaskana* Sarg.) and trembling aspen (*Populus tremuloides* Michx.) in the interior and Southcentral lowlands, Lutz spruce (*P. × lutzii* Little) on the Kenai Peninsula and Sitka spruce (*P. sitchensis* (Bong.) Carrière) along the coast. The validation strip was the Talkeetna to Byers Lake stretch of the Susitna valley, between `r sprintf("%.1f", sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(used, 4326))["ymin"])`° N and `r sprintf("%.1f", sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(used, 4326))["ymax"])`° N along the Parks Highway, where @Zwieback_2024 delineated dead spruce crowns on a WorldView-2 image of 2 August 2021 and the outbreak arrived around 2016. The map was tested in four regions, the Kenai Peninsula Borough, where the 1990s outbreak ran and a new one has followed, the Matanuska-Susitna Borough holding the strip, the Valdez-Cordova census area holding the Copper River basin, which the outbreak reached last, and the Denali, Fairbanks North Star and Southeast Fairbanks areas of the Interior, which the outbreak's northern front entered along the Nenana River in the Denali Borough from 2020. Within the frame of the strip the survey mapped spruce beetle damage on `r format(round(sum(as.numeric(sf::st_area(ads[ads$SURVEY_YEAR == 2018, ]))) / 1e4), big.mark = ",")` ha in 2018, the largest area of any year.

```{r}
#| label: fig-spread
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: "Area of spruce beetle damage mapped by the aerial detection survey across Alaska in each survey year, by quarter-degree band of latitude, on a square-root colour scale; the dashed lines bound the latitudes of the frame of Figure 1."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.6
# USFS Forest Health Protection aerial detection survey damage areas, Alaska Region 10, all years.
# https://www.fs.usda.gov/foresthealth/docs/IDS_Data_for_Download/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb.zip
spread_csv <- "03.outputs/survey_by_latitude.csv"
if (!file.exists(spread_csv)) {
  pg <- sf::st_read("02.inputs/ids-region10/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb", quiet = TRUE,
                    query = "SELECT SURVEY_YEAR, Shape FROM DAMAGE_AREAS_FLAT_AllYears_AK_Rgn10 WHERE DCA_CODE = 11009 AND SURVEY_YEAR <= 2024")
  pg <- data.frame(year = pg$SURVEY_YEAR, ha = as.numeric(sf::st_area(pg)) / 1e4,
                   lat = sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(sf::st_centroid(sf::st_geometry(pg)), 4326))[, 2])
  write.csv(aggregate(ha ~ year + band, transform(pg, band = floor(lat * 4) / 4), sum), spread_csv, row.names = FALSE)
}
spread <- read.csv(spread_csv); by_year <- aggregate(ha ~ year, spread, sum)
north <- function(y) 100 * sum(spread$ha[spread$year %in% y & spread$band >= 61]) / sum(spread$ha[spread$year %in% y])
ggplot(spread, aes(year, band + 0.125, fill = ha / 1000)) + geom_tile() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(frame, 4326))[c(2, 4)], linetype = "22", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c("Thousand ha", option = "inferno", direction = -1, trans = "sqrt") + labs(x = NULL, y = "Latitude (° N)") + th
```

Across Alaska the survey mapped the most spruce beetle damage in `r by_year$year[which.max(by_year$ha)]`, `r format(round(max(by_year$ha)), big.mark = ",")` ha, and the least in `r by_year$year[which.min(by_year$ha)]`, `r format(round(min(by_year$ha)), big.mark = ",")` ha, and `r sprintf("%.0f", north(2016:2024))` per cent of the area mapped from 2016 to 2024 lay north of 61° N against `r sprintf("%.0f", north(1997:2015))` per cent of the area mapped from `r min(spread$year)` to 2015 (@fig-spread).

# Data

## Reference data

The reference data were the dead spruce crown polygons that @Zwieback_2024 delineated by hand to train and test their network, released as an extent and a set of crowns for each of `r sum(areas$set == "training")` training areas of 512 m and `r sum(areas$set == "test")` test areas of 90 m, and their severity map, the dead crown fraction of each 90 m cell of a strip of the valley mapped from the same image. The areas delineated on the pre-outbreak image of 14 July 2013 hold `r sum(areas$crowns[areas$year == 2013])` crowns between them and were set aside, leaving the `r sum(used$set == "training")` training areas and `r sum(used$set == "test")` test areas delineated on the image of 2 August 2021, which hold `r format(sum(used$crowns[used$set == "training"]), big.mark = ",")` and `r format(sum(used$crowns[used$set == "test"]), big.mark = ",")` crowns. The crowns record where a spruce stood dead on that date and not when it died, and the delineators could not separate species or mortality agent, so a crown is a dead spruce in an area of beetle outbreak rather than a confirmed beetle kill. Each area was divided into 10 m cells on the WGS 84 UTM zone 5N grid of the labels, `r format(nrow(cells), big.mark = ",")` cells in all, and the fraction of each cell covered by dead crowns was computed. The aerial detection survey damage polygons of the Forest Service for Alaska, all years, gave the second label, each polygon carrying its survey year, host and mortality class, and the surveyed-area polygons gave the ground the observers flew over. The Forest Inventory and Analysis plot and tree tables for Alaska [@Bechtold_2005] gave the ground check, every live or standing dead white spruce with its diameter and height.

## Satellite data

```{r}
#| label: s1-flatten
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Sentinel-1 GRD, Earth Engine COPERNICUS/S1_GRD.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/COPERNICUS_S1_GRD
# Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, Earth Engine COPERNICUS/DEM/GLO30_2024_1.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/COPERNICUS_DEM_GLO30_2024_1
s1 <- ee$ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/S1_GRD")$filter(ee$Filter$eq("instrumentMode", "IW"))$
  filter(ee$Filter$listContains("transmitterReceiverPolarisation", "VH"))
dem <- ee$ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/DEM/GLO30_2024_1")$select("DEM")$mosaic()
rad <- pi / 180
flatten <- function(img, bands = c("VV", "VH"), smooth = TRUE) {  # volume-model slope correction of Vollrath et al. (2020), layover and shadow masked; smooth applies the 3 by 3 mean
  theta <- img$select("angle")$multiply(rad)
  phi <- ee$Image$constant(ee$Terrain$aspect(img$select("angle"))$reduceRegion(ee$Reducer$mean(), img$geometry(), 1000)$get("aspect"))$multiply(rad)
  a_r <- ee$Terrain$slope(dem)$multiply(rad)$tan()$multiply(phi$subtract(ee$Terrain$aspect(dem)$multiply(rad))$cos())$atan()
  g0 <- ee$Image$constant(10)$pow(img$select(bands)$divide(10))$divide(theta$cos())
  corr <- ee$Image$constant(pi / 2)$subtract(theta)$add(a_r)$tan()$divide(ee$Image$constant(pi / 2)$subtract(theta)$tan())
  g <- g0$divide(corr); if (smooth) g <- g$focalMean(1.5)
  ee$Image(g$log10()$multiply(10)$updateMask(a_r$lt(theta)$And(a_r$gt(theta$subtract(pi / 2))))$
    copyProperties(img, list("system:time_start", "relativeOrbitNumber_start")))
}
```

Sentinel-1 ground range detected scenes acquired in interferometric wide swath mode were read in Google Earth Engine [@Gorelick_2017], where each scene had been corrected for thermal noise, radiometrically calibrated, terrain corrected and converted to decibels. Following the analysis-ready data preparation of @Mullissa_2021, the backscatter was normalised for slope with the volume scattering model of @Vollrath_2020, using the Copernicus 30 m digital elevation model in place of the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission, which does not extend north of 60° N, and pixels in layover or radar shadow were masked. Speckle was reduced with a 3 by 3 pixel mean in linear power before conversion back to decibels. The validation strip is imaged by two relative orbits, the ascending orbit 65 and the descending orbit 131, which view the forest from opposite sides at different incidence angles, so the two were kept apart in the validation and pooled, after a correction for incidence angle, in the statewide map. Three canopy height estimates were read beside the radar. The ETH canopy height of 2020 is a 10 m model of GEDI lidar heights fitted to Sentinel-2 imagery [@Lang_2023]; two estimates independent of any model were taken as a surface model minus the 10 m terrain model of the USGS 3D Elevation Program, the surface being the Copernicus GLO-30 model, an X-band radar surface of 2011 to 2015, and the ArcticDEM version 4 mosaic, an optical stereo surface at 2 m [@Porter_2023]. The JAXA ALOS PALSAR yearly mosaics gave L-band HH and HV at 25 m [@Shimada_2014], the LANDFIRE existing vegetation type of Alaska gave the vegetation class of each cell [@Rollins_2009], and the ABoVE conifer top cover of 2020 [@Macander_2022] defined living forest in the labels.

# Methods

## Literature review

```{r}
#| label: review-terms
#| echo: true
#| output: false
terms_csv <- "04.references/review/search-terms.csv"
if (!file.exists(terms_csv)) {  # every candidate term from the title and keywords, selected by hand in the file and frozen with the protocol
  front <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter("01.manuscript/manuscript.qmd")
  small <- c("a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "by", "do", "does", "for", "from", "how", "in", "into", "is", "its", "of", "on", "or", "the", "to", "under", "using", "versus", "what", "why", "with", "across")
  phrases <- function(x) x |> stringr::str_to_lower() |> stringr::str_remove_all("[*_]") |> stringr::str_replace_all("[^[:alnum:][:space:]-]", " | ") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all(paste0("\\b(", paste(small, collapse = "|"), ")\\b"), " | ") |> stringr::str_split_1("\\|") |> stringr::str_squish() |> purrr::keep(function(p) nchar(p) > 2)
  dir.create(dirname(terms_csv), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(term = stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_to_lower(unlist(front$keywords))), source = "keywords"), tibble::tibble(term = phrases(front$title), source = "title")) |>
    dplyr::distinct(term, .keep_all = TRUE) |> dplyr::mutate(question = NA, concept = NA) |> readr::write_csv(terms_csv, na = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-queries
#| echo: true
#| output: false
front <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter("01.manuscript/manuscript.qmd")
declared <- stringr::str_to_lower(paste(front$title, paste(unlist(front$keywords), collapse = " ")))
term_regex <- function(x) if (stringr::str_ends(x, "\\*")) paste0("\\b", stringr::str_escape(stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$"))) else paste0("\\b", stringr::str_escape(x), "\\b")
terms <- readr::read_csv(terms_csv, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(question), !is.na(concept)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(term = stringr::str_to_lower(term)) |> tidyr::separate_longer_delim(question, " ")
stray <- terms$term[!purrr::map_lgl(terms$term, function(x) stringr::str_detect(declared, term_regex(x)))]
if (nrow(terms) == 0) stop("No search terms selected in ", terms_csv)
if (length(stray) > 0) stop("Not in the title or keywords: ", paste(unique(stray), collapse = ", "))  # a new word enters the search only by entering the keywords first
queries <- terms |> dplyr::summarise(.by = c(question, concept), group = paste(term, collapse = "|")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = question, route = paste(c(dplyr::first(question), concept), collapse = "-"), concepts = paste(group, collapse = " AND "))
```

```{r}
#| label: review-store
#| echo: true
#| output: false
store_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/review-store-hits.csv"; log_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv"
if (!file.exists(store_csv)) {
  # library-science manifest and source notes, the central store at Github/library-science, https://github.com/seamusrobertmurphy/library-science
  manifest <- readr::read_csv("../library-science/library/manifest.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
  notes <- tibble::tibble(path = list.files("../library-science/sources", "\\.md$", full.names = TRUE)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(key = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(path)), note = purrr::map_chr(path, function(p) paste(readLines(p, warn = FALSE), collapse = " ")))
  store <- manifest |> dplyr::filter(status %in% c("verified", "filed", "unverified"), !is.na(title) | !is.na(key)) |> dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(notes, key, note), by = "key") |> dplyr::mutate(text = stringr::str_to_lower(paste(title, note)))
  term_pat <- function(x) if (stringr::str_ends(x, "\\*")) paste0(stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$"), "\\w*") else paste0(x, "\\b")
  hits <- purrr::pmap(queries, function(question, route, concepts) {
    patterns <- purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND "), function(g) paste0("\\b(", paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), term_pat), collapse = "|"), ")"))
    keep <- purrr::reduce(purrr::map(patterns, function(r) stringr::str_detect(store$text, r)), `&`)
    store[keep, ] |> dplyr::transmute(question, route = paste0("store-", route), key, doi, title, year, venue = container, source_note = dplyr::if_else(has_source_note == "yes", key, NA)) }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
  readr::write_csv(hits, store_csv)
  queries |> dplyr::transmute(strand = "library-science", route = paste0("store-", route), query = concepts, date = as.character(Sys.Date())) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::count(hits, route, name = "retrieved"), by = "route") |> dplyr::mutate(retrieved = tidyr::replace_na(retrieved, 0L), reported_total = retrieved, cap = NA, capped = FALSE, error = NA) |> readr::write_csv(log_csv)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-semantic-scholar
#| echo: true
#| output: false
s2_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/review-s2-hits.csv"
if (!file.exists(s2_csv)) {
  search_s2 <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 3000) {
    query <- paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND "), function(g) paste0("(", paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), function(x) if (grepl(" ", x)) paste0('"', x, '"') else x), collapse = " | "), ")")), collapse = " + ")
    papers <- list(); token <- NULL; total <- NA
    repeat {
      # Semantic Scholar Academic Graph bulk search, https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/graph#tag/Paper-Data/operation/get_graph_paper_bulk_search
      body <- httr2::request("https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search/bulk") |> httr2::req_url_query(query = query, fields = "title,year,venue,externalIds,citationCount,publicationTypes,abstract", token = token) |>
        httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 10, backoff = function(i) 5 * i) |> httr2::req_perform() |> httr2::resp_body_json()
      total <- body$total; token <- body$token; papers <- c(papers, body$data); Sys.sleep(1.5)
      if (is.null(token) || length(papers) >= cap) break }
    works <- purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(papers, function(w) tibble::tibble(doi = w$externalIds$DOI %||% NA_character_, title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$year %||% NA_integer_, venue = w$venue %||% NA_character_, type = paste(unlist(w$publicationTypes), collapse = " "), citations = w$citationCount %||% NA_integer_, abstract = w$abstract %||% NA_character_)))
    list(hits = dplyr::mutate(works, question, route = paste0("s2-", route), .before = 1), log = tibble::tibble(strand = "semantic-scholar", route = paste0("s2-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = nrow(works), reported_total = total, cap, capped = total > cap, error = NA)) }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(queries, search_s2)
  readr::write_csv(purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(runs, "hits")), s2_csv)
  readr::read_csv(log_csv, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |> dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(runs, "log")) |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.character))) |> readr::write_csv(log_csv)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-openalex
#| echo: true
#| output: false
oa_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/review-openalex-hits.csv"
if (!file.exists(oa_csv)) {
  stems <- c("susceptib*" = "susceptible OR susceptibility", "map*" = "map OR mapping OR mapped OR maps")  # OpenAlex takes no wildcard, so each stem is written out
  search_oa <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 3000) {
    query <- paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND "), function(g) paste0("(", paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), function(x) if (x %in% names(stems)) stems[[x]] else if (grepl(" ", x)) paste0('"', x, '"') else x), collapse = " OR "), ")")), collapse = " AND ")
    works <- list(); cursor <- "*"; total <- NA
    repeat {
      # OpenAlex works search, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/search-works
      body <- httr2::request("https://api.openalex.org/works") |> httr2::req_url_query(filter = paste0("title_and_abstract.search:", query), `per-page` = 200, cursor = cursor, mailto = "seamusrobertmurphy@gmail.com", select = "id,doi,title,publication_year,type,cited_by_count,primary_location,abstract_inverted_index") |>
        httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 8, backoff = function(i) 5 * i, is_transient = function(r) httr2::resp_status(r) %in% c(401, 429, 500, 503)) |> httr2::req_perform() |> httr2::resp_body_json()  # titles and abstracts, the same scope as the Semantic Scholar strand; a 401 from OpenAlex has been transient
      total <- body$meta$count; cursor <- body$meta$next_cursor; works <- c(works, body$results); Sys.sleep(0.5)
      if (is.null(cursor) || length(body$results) == 0 || length(works) >= cap) break }
    abstract <- function(ii) if (is.null(ii)) NA_character_ else { pos <- unlist(ii, use.names = FALSE); paste(rep(names(ii), lengths(ii))[order(pos)], collapse = " ") }  # the inverted index back into the abstract
    hits <- purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(works, function(w) tibble::tibble(doi = if (is.null(w$doi)) NA_character_ else sub("^https://doi.org/", "", w$doi), title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$publication_year %||% NA_integer_,
      venue = w$primary_location$source$display_name %||% NA_character_, type = w$type %||% NA_character_, citations = w$cited_by_count %||% NA_integer_, abstract = abstract(w$abstract_inverted_index))))
    list(hits = dplyr::mutate(hits, question, route = paste0("oa-", route), .before = 1), log = tibble::tibble(strand = "openalex", route = paste0("oa-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = nrow(hits), reported_total = total, cap, capped = total > cap, error = NA)) }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(queries, search_oa)
  readr::write_csv(purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(runs, "hits")), oa_csv)
  readr::read_csv(log_csv, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |> dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(runs, "log")) |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.character))) |> readr::write_csv(log_csv)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-chase
#| echo: true
#| output: false
central <- c("10.1139/x83-097", "10.1093/forestscience/31.4.839", "10.1139/x94-268", "10.1139/x83-014", "10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2024.05.013")  # Hard et al. 1983, Hard 1985, Reynolds and Holsten 1994, Werner and Holsten 1983, Zwieback et al. 2024
chase_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/review-chase-hits.csv"
if (length(central) > 0 && !file.exists(chase_csv)) {
  chase <- function(seed_doi, direction) {
    # Semantic Scholar Academic Graph references and citations, https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/graph#tag/Paper-Data
    resp <- httr2::request(paste0("https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/DOI:", seed_doi, "/", direction)) |> httr2::req_url_query(fields = "title,year,venue,externalIds,abstract", limit = 1000) |>
      httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 10, backoff = function(i) 5 * i) |> httr2::req_error(is_error = function(r) httr2::resp_status(r) == 429) |> httr2::req_perform(); Sys.sleep(1.5)
    if (httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200) return(tibble::tibble(seed = seed_doi, route = paste0("chase-", direction), error = httr2::resp_status_desc(resp)))
    key <- if (direction == "references") "citedPaper" else "citingPaper"
    purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(httr2::resp_body_json(resp)$data, function(w) tibble::tibble(doi = w[[key]]$externalIds$DOI %||% NA_character_, title = w[[key]]$title %||% NA_character_, year = w[[key]]$year %||% NA_integer_, venue = w[[key]]$venue %||% NA_character_, abstract = w[[key]]$abstract %||% NA_character_))) |>
      dplyr::mutate(seed = seed_doi, route = paste0("chase-", direction), .before = 1) }
  readr::write_csv(purrr::list_rbind(purrr::pmap(tidyr::expand_grid(seed_doi = central, direction = c("references", "citations")), chase)), chase_csv)
}
```

The literature review was run against the two objectives under the protocol frozen in `04.references/review/protocol.md` on 14 October 2026, with one review question on the tree and stand attributes that predict attack, one on the remote sensing of spruce beetle damage and susceptibility, and one on whether a susceptibility map had been made from satellite structure data before. Search terms were drawn from the manuscript's title and keywords and joined into queries of two or three concepts. Three strands were searched on 14 October 2026, the central store of the author's reading, the Semantic Scholar bulk search and OpenAlex, with the Forest Service Treesearch repository and the archive.org scans of the Forest Service reports of 1954 to 1977 searched by hand. Records were joined on their digital object identifier or title and read on title and abstract by one reader, and every exclusion carries a coded reason. One round of backward and forward citation chasing ran from the five central records named in the code. Every record behind a direction in @tbl-attributes was read in full where the full text could be reached; the full texts of the Canadian Journal of Forest Research papers of 1983 to 2004 could not be reached from the author's machine, so those papers are cited for what their abstracts state and for nothing else.

## Stand validation

```{r}
#| label: s1-samples
#| echo: true
#| output: false
samp_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/tile_samples"
months <- seq(as.Date("2017-06-01"), as.Date("2021-08-01"), by = "month"); ym <- format(months, "%Y%m"); orbits <- c(65L, 131L)
composite <- function(col, bands, o, g, m) col$filterBounds(g)$filter(ee$Filter$eq("relativeOrbitNumber_start", o))$  # the median of the slope-corrected scenes of one orbit in one month
  filterDate(format(m), format(seq(m, by = "month", length.out = 2)[2]))$map(function(img) flatten(img, bands))$median()$rename(paste0(bands, o, "_", format(m, "%Y%m")))
sample_areas <- function(dir, comps) {  # sampled at the centre of every 10 m cell of every label area, one file per area
  dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(used))) {
    out <- file.path(dir, paste0(used$roi[i], ".csv")); if (file.exists(out)) next
    xy <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(used$geometry[i], 4326))
    g <- ee$Geometry$Polygon(list(lapply(seq_len(nrow(xy)), function(k) c(xy[k, 1], xy[k, 2]))))
    f <- tryCatch(ee$Image$cat(comps(g))$sample(region = g, scale = 10, projection = "EPSG:32605", geometries = TRUE, dropNulls = FALSE)$getInfo()$features,
                  error = function(e) if (grepl("concurren|Too Many Requests|timed out|memory", conditionMessage(e))) NULL else stop(e))
    if (is.null(f)) next  # left for the next pass when Earth Engine refuses the request under load
    p <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(data.frame(t(sapply(f, function(z) unlist(z$geometry$coordinates)))), coords = 1:2, crs = 4326), 32605))
    write.csv(data.frame(roi = used$roi[i], x = round((p[, 1] - 5) / 10) * 10 + 5, y = round((p[, 2] - 5) / 10) * 10 + 5,
                         dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(f, function(z) Filter(Negate(is.null), z$properties)))), out, row.names = FALSE)
  }
}
spec <- expand.grid(o = orbits, m = format(months), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sample_areas(samp_dir, function(g) unname(Map(function(o, m) composite(s1, c("VV", "VH"), o, g, as.Date(m)), spec$o, spec$m)))
```

For every month from June 2017 to August 2021, the month of the label image, the median slope-corrected backscatter of each orbit and polarisation was composited in Earth Engine and sampled at the centre of every 10 m cell of every label area, on the same UTM zone 5N grid as the labels.

```{r}
#| label: s1-samples-pre
#| echo: true
#| output: false
months_pre <- seq(as.Date("2014-10-01"), as.Date("2017-05-01"), by = "month")
s1_all <- ee$ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/S1_GRD")$filter(ee$Filter$eq("instrumentMode", "IW"))$filter(ee$Filter$listContains("transmitterReceiverPolarisation", "VV"))  # every scene carries VV, only the dual-polarised scenes carry VH
spec_pre <- expand.grid(b = c("VV", "VH"), o = orbits, m = format(months_pre), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sample_areas("02.inputs/derived/tile_samples_pre", function(g) unname(Map(function(b, o, m) composite(if (b == "VV") s1_all else s1, b, o, g, as.Date(m)), spec_pre$b, spec_pre$o, spec_pre$m)))
```

Before June 2017 only the ascending orbit carried dual-polarised scenes over the areas, while scenes with VV alone were acquired on both orbits in most months from October 2014, so for October 2014 to May 2017 the VV backscatter of every scene was composited and sampled in the same way.

```{r}
#| label: series
#| echo: true
#| output: false
bands <- paste0(c("VV", "VH"), rep(orbits, each = 2))
samples <- merge(cells, dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(list.files(samp_dir, "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE), read.csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character"))), by = c("roi", "x", "y"))
months_seen <- sapply(orbits, function(o) length(grep(paste0("^VV", o, "_"), names(samples))))
cube <- array(NA_real_, c(nrow(samples), length(ym), length(bands)), list(NULL, ym, bands))
for (b in bands) { has <- intersect(paste0(b, "_", ym), names(samples)); cube[, sub(".*_", "", has), b] <- as.matrix(samples[, has]) }
samples <- cbind(samples[, c("roi", "set", "x", "y", "dead")], setNames(as.data.frame(sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(samples[, c("x", "y")], coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605), 4326))), c("lon", "lat")))
gaps <- mean(is.na(cube))
fill <- function(v) if (sum(!is.na(v)) < 2) v else approx(seq_along(v), v, seq_along(v), rule = 2)$y  # linear interpolation across months without a scene
cube <- aperm(apply(cube, c(1, 3), fill), c(2, 1, 3))
complete <- rowSums(is.na(cube)) == 0
window <- 24L; intervals <- c(1L, 2L, 3L, 6L)
series <- function(end, k = 1L, rows = seq_len(nrow(samples))) {  # the 24 months ending in `end`, averaged over blocks of k months
  j <- (match(end, ym) - window + 1):match(end, ym); blocks <- rep(seq_len(window / k), each = k); x <- cube[rows, j, , drop = FALSE]
  if (k > 1) x <- aperm(apply(x, c(1, 3), function(v) tapply(v, blocks, mean)), c(2, 1, 3))
  list(x = x, dates = months[j][!duplicated(blocks)])
}
as_sits <- function(rows, s) {  # a sits sample table, one time series per cell
  tb <- tibble::tibble(longitude = samples$lon[rows], latitude = samples$lat[rows], start_date = s$dates[1], end_date = tail(s$dates, 1),
                       label = ifelse(samples$dead[rows] >= 0.1, "dead", "alive"), cube = "S1",
                       time_series = lapply(seq_along(rows), function(i) tibble::as_tibble(cbind(data.frame(Index = s$dates), s$x[i, , ]))))
  class(tb) <- c("sits", class(tb)); tb
}
```

```{r}
#| label: folds
#| echo: true
#| output: false
train <- samples$set == "training"; use <- (samples$dead >= 0.1 | samples$dead == 0) & complete
ctr <- sf::st_as_sf(aggregate(cbind(x, y) ~ roi, samples[train, ], mean), coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605)
folds <- blockCV::cv_spatial(ctr, k = 5, size = 15000, selection = "random", seed = 20260915, progress = FALSE, report = FALSE, plot = FALSE)
samples$fold <- folds$folds_ids[match(samples$roi, ctr$roi)]
```

```{r}
#| label: stands
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# ABoVE modelled top cover by plant functional type, conifer top cover 2020 (Macander and Nelson 2022), ORNL DAAC https://doi.org/10.3334/ORNLDAAC/2032, row `covariates/` of 02.inputs/README.md.
org <- aggregate(cbind(x0 = x, y0 = y) ~ roi, samples, min)
samples$stand <- paste(samples$roi, (samples$x - org$x0[match(samples$roi, org$roi)]) %/% 90, (samples$y - org$y0[match(samples$roi, org$roi)]) %/% 90)
g <- samples$stand %in% names(which(table(samples$stand) == 81))  # the 90 m cells wholly inside their area
stands <- aggregate(cbind(x, y, dead) ~ stand + roi + set, samples[g, ], mean); stands$fold <- samples$fold[match(stands$roi, samples$roi)]
ll <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(stands, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605), 4326)); stands$lon <- ll[, 1]; stands$lat <- ll[, 2]
sq <- sf::st_buffer(sf::st_as_sf(stands, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605), 45, endCapStyle = "SQUARE")
conifer <- terra::rast("02.inputs/covariates/conifer_topcover_2020.tif"); sq <- terra::vect(sf::st_transform(sq, terra::crs(conifer)))
stands$conifer <- terra::extract(terra::crop(conifer, terra::ext(sq) + 100), sq, fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE, ID = FALSE)[, 1]
stands$label <- ifelse(stands$dead >= 0.01, "dead", ifelse(stands$dead == 0 & stands$conifer >= 5, "alive", NA))  # living forest is a stand with no dead crown and conifer top cover of 5 per cent or more
pre <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(list.files("02.inputs/derived/tile_samples_pre", "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE), read.csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character")))
pre <- pre[match(paste(samples$roi, samples$x, samples$y), paste(pre$roi, pre$x, pre$y)), ]
ym_all <- format(seq(as.Date("2014-10-01"), as.Date("2021-08-01"), by = "month"), "%Y%m")
lin_mean <- function(M) { M <- as.matrix(M); 10 * log10(rowsum(10^(M / 10), samples$stand[g], na.rm = TRUE) / rowsum((!is.na(M)) + 0, samples$stand[g])) }  # the stand mean in linear power
scube <- array(NA_real_, c(nrow(stands), length(ym_all), length(bands)), list(stands$stand, ym_all, bands))
for (b in bands) { P <- pre[g, grep(paste0("^", b, "_"), names(pre)), drop = FALSE]; names(P) <- sub(".*_", "", names(P))
  M <- lin_mean(cbind(P, setNames(as.data.frame(cube[g, , b]), ym))); scube[, colnames(M), b] <- M[stands$stand, ] }
scube <- aperm(apply(scube, c(1, 3), fill), c(2, 1, 3))
```

```{r}
#| label: tempcnn-stands
#| echo: true
#| output: false
spred_csv <- "03.outputs/stand_predictions.csv"
designs <- list(VV_2014 = list(bands = c("VV65", "VV131"), from = "201410"), all_2017 = list(bands = bands, from = "201706"))
steps <- function(d) match(d$from, ym_all):length(ym_all)
ok_st <- function(d) rowSums(is.na(scube[, steps(d), d$bands, drop = FALSE])) == 0
as_sits_st <- function(rows, d) { j <- steps(d); dates <- as.Date(paste0(ym_all[j], "01"), "%Y%m%d")
  tb <- tibble::tibble(longitude = stands$lon[rows], latitude = stands$lat[rows], start_date = dates[1], end_date = tail(dates, 1), label = dplyr::coalesce(stands$label[rows], "alive"), cube = "S1",
                       time_series = lapply(rows, function(i) tibble::as_tibble(cbind(data.frame(Index = dates), scube[i, j, d$bands]))))
  class(tb) <- c("sits", class(tb)); tb }
fit_st <- function(rows, d) { set.seed(20260915); sits::sits_train(as_sits_st(rows, d), sits::sits_tempcnn(epochs = 60L, patience = 10L, seed = 20260915L, verbose = FALSE)) }
p_dead_st <- function(m, rows, d) sapply(sits::sits_classify(as_sits_st(rows, d), m, multicores = 1L, progress = FALSE)$predicted, function(z) z$dead)
if (!file.exists(spred_csv)) { torch::torch_manual_seed(20260915); out <- list()
  for (nm in names(designs)) { d <- designs[[nm]]; ok <- ok_st(d); lab <- ok & !is.na(stands$label); tr <- stands$set == "training"
    for (f in 1:5) { m <- fit_st(which(lab & tr & stands$fold != f), d); te <- which(ok & tr & stands$fold == f)
      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(stands[te, c("stand", "roi", "set", "fold", "dead", "conifer")], design = nm, p_dead = p_dead_st(m, te, d)) }
    m <- fit_st(which(lab & tr), d); te <- which(ok & !tr)
    out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(stands[te, c("stand", "roi", "set", "fold", "dead", "conifer")], design = nm, p_dead = p_dead_st(m, te, d)) }
  write.csv(do.call(rbind, out), spred_csv, row.names = FALSE) }
```

```{r}
#| label: accuracy-stands
#| echo: true
#| output: false
auc <- function(x, y) { r <- rank(x); n1 <- sum(y); (sum(r[y]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * (length(y) - n1)) }  # the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, from the ranks
sp <- read.csv(spred_csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character")); sp$hit <- sp$p_dead >= 0.5
sp$label <- ifelse(sp$dead >= 0.01, TRUE, ifelse(sp$dead == 0 & sp$conifer >= 5, FALSE, NA))
score_st <- function(d) { d <- d[!is.na(d$label), ]; tp <- sum(d$hit & d$label)
  c(dead = sum(d$label), alive = sum(!d$label), precision = tp / sum(d$hit), recall = tp / sum(d$label), F1 = 2 * tp / (sum(d$hit) + sum(d$label)), AUC = auc(d$p_dead, d$label)) }
sacc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(sp, list(sp$design, sp$set)), function(d) data.frame(design = d$design[1], set = d$set[1], t(score_st(d)))))
sp$bin <- ifelse(sp$dead == 0, ifelse(sp$conifer >= 5, "Living forest", "No conifer"), as.character(cut(sp$dead, c(0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 1), c("0 to 0.01", "0.01 to 0.02", "0.02 to 0.05", "0.05 to 0.1", "0.1 to 1"))))
sfloor <- with(sp[sp$set == "training", ], tapply(hit, list(bin, design), mean)); sfloor_n <- with(sp[sp$set == "training" & sp$design == "VV_2014", ], table(bin))
sbase <- sapply(designs, function(d) { r <- ok_st(d) & !is.na(stands$label) & stands$set == "training"; sapply(d$bands, function(b) auc(rowMeans(scube[r, steps(d), b]), stands$label[r] == "dead")) })  # one band averaged over the design's months, with no training
write.csv(sacc, "03.outputs/stand_accuracy.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: change-stands
#| echo: true
#| output: false
era <- function(a, b) which(ym_all >= a & ym_all <= b)
lab_st <- !is.na(stands$label) & stands$set == "training"; dead_st <- stands$label == "dead"
chg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("VV65", "VV131", "VH65"), function(b) data.frame(stand = stands$stand, band = b, dead = dead_st, labelled = lab_st, conifer = stands$conifer,  # VH on orbit 65 rests on the 11 dual-polarised months before June 2017, VH on orbit 131 has none
  pre = rowMeans(scube[, era("201410", "201612"), b]), late = rowMeans(scube[, era("201906", "202108"), b]))))  # each stand against its own level before the outbreak reached the area
chg$change <- chg$late - chg$pre
change <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(chg[chg$labelled, ], chg$band[chg$labelled]), function(d) data.frame(band = d$band[1],
  auc_pre = auc(d$pre, d$dead), auc_late = auc(d$late, d$dead), auc_change = auc(d$change, d$dead), auc_conifer = auc(d$conifer, d$dead),
  change_dead = mean(d$change[d$dead]), change_alive = mean(d$change[!d$dead]), t = unname(t.test(d$change[d$dead], d$change[!d$dead])$statistic), df = unname(t.test(d$change[d$dead], d$change[!d$dead])$parameter), p = t.test(d$change[d$dead], d$change[!d$dead])$p.value)))
write.csv(change, "03.outputs/stand_change.csv", row.names = FALSE)  # read by the abstract, which renders before this chunk
```

The validation was made at the scale at which @Zwieback_2024 reported severity. Each 512 m label area was divided into 90 m cells on the UTM zone 5N grid, and the `r format(nrow(stands), big.mark = ",")` cells wholly inside their area, each holding 81 of the 10 m cells, took the mean dead crown fraction and the mean backscatter of those cells, the mean being taken in linear power. A stand was dead at a dead crown fraction of 0.01 or more and living at a fraction of 0 with conifer top cover of 5 per cent or more, so that the living class held forest and not treeless ground. For each stand the mean VV level of October 2014 to December 2016, before the aerial survey recorded spruce beetle damage in any label area, was set against the mean of June 2019 to August 2021, and the level of the early period, the level of the late period and the change between them were each scored by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for dead against living stands, with a Welch t-test on the change, so that a difference that existed before the outbreak could be told from a change the outbreak made. As a check that a trained model would add nothing to the level, the temporal convolutional network of @Pelletier_2019 as implemented in the sits package [@Simoes_2021] was trained on the full monthly series of each stand, with the `r nrow(ctr)` training areas dealt to five spatial folds over 15 km hexagons with blockCV [@Valavi_2019] so that no stand was scored by a network that had seen its area, and scored by F1 and the area under the curve beside the untrained mean of one band.

## Landscape validation

```{r}
#| label: landscape
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Zwieback (2023) spruce beetle outbreak severity, Southcentral Alaska 2021, 90 m, Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8423568, no licence declared, validation use only (row `zwieback-severity/` of 02.inputs/README.md).
sev <- terra::trim(terra::rast("02.inputs/zwieback-severity/merged_ref_h_c90c.tif"))
land_tif <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_s1_levels.tif"
if (!file.exists(land_tif)) {
  eras <- list(pre = c("2014-10-01", "2017-01-01"), late = c("2019-06-01", "2021-09-01"))
  level <- function(o, e) s1_all$filter(ee$Filter$eq("relativeOrbitNumber_start", o))$filterDate(eras[[e]][1], eras[[e]][2])$map(function(img) flatten(img, "VV"))$mean()$rename(paste0("VV", o, "_", e))  # the mean slope-corrected VV of every scene of one orbit in one era
  img <- ee$Image$cat(unname(Map(level, rep(orbits, 2), rep(names(eras), each = 2))))$setDefaultProjection("EPSG:32605", NULL, 10)$reduceResolution(ee$Reducer$mean(), maxPixels = 256L)  # the 81 cells of 10 m averaged into each 90 m cell
  e <- as.vector(terra::ext(sev)); rows <- split(seq_len(nrow(sev)), ceiling(seq_len(nrow(sev)) / 10))
  tile_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_tiles"; dir.create(tile_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (r in rows) { f <- file.path(tile_dir, sprintf("rows_%03d.tif", min(r))); if (file.exists(f)) next  # ten rows per request, on the grid of the severity map, kept so that a failed run resumes
    url <- img$getDownloadURL(list(crs = "EPSG:32605", crs_transform = c(90, 0, e[1], 0, -90, e[4] - (min(r) - 1) * 90), dimensions = c(ncol(sev), length(r)), format = "GEO_TIFF", filePerBand = FALSE))
    for (attempt in 1:4) if (inherits(try(download.file(url, f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE), silent = TRUE), "try-error")) { unlink(f); Sys.sleep(30) } else break  # Earth Engine refuses a request now and then under load
    if (!file.exists(f)) stop("tile ", f, " did not download") }
  terra::writeRaster(terra::merge(terra::sprc(lapply(list.files(tile_dir, "^rows_.*\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE), terra::rast))), land_tif) }
lv <- terra::rast(land_tif); names(lv) <- paste0("VV", rep(orbits, 2), "_", rep(c("pre", "late"), each = 2))  # the GeoTIFF carries no band names
```

```{r}
#| label: landscape-test
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# USFS Forest Health Protection aerial detection survey damage areas, Alaska Region 10, all years.
# https://www.fs.usda.gov/foresthealth/docs/IDS_Data_for_Download/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb.zip
con90 <- terra::project(terra::crop(conifer, terra::project(terra::as.polygons(terra::ext(lv), crs = "EPSG:32605"), terra::crs(conifer))), lv, method = "average")
surv <- sf::st_read("02.inputs/ids-region10/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb", quiet = TRUE, query = "SELECT SURVEY_YEAR, Shape FROM DAMAGE_AREAS_FLAT_AllYears_AK_Rgn10 WHERE DCA_CODE = 11009 AND SURVEY_YEAR BETWEEN 2017 AND 2024")
in_surv <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(sf::st_transform(surv, 32605)), lv, field = 1, background = 0)
land <- na.omit(data.frame(sev = terra::values(terra::resample(sev, lv, method = "near"))[, 1], terra::values(lv), conifer = terra::values(con90)[, 1], survey = terra::values(in_surv)[, 1]))
land$class <- ifelse(land$sev >= 0.01, "dead", ifelse(land$sev == 0 & land$conifer >= 5, "alive", NA)); lab_l <- !is.na(land$class); dead_l <- land$class == "dead"
forest_l <- land$conifer >= 5
land_auc <- sapply(c("VV65", "VV131"), function(b) c(level = auc(land[[paste0(b, "_pre")]][lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]), change = auc((land[[paste0(b, "_late")]] - land[[paste0(b, "_pre")]])[lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]),
  rho = cor(land[[paste0(b, "_pre")]][forest_l], land$sev[forest_l], method = "spearman"), survey = auc(land[[paste0(b, "_pre")]][forest_l], land$survey[forest_l] == 1)))
land_bins <- with(land[forest_l, ], tapply(VV131_pre, cut(sev, c(-1, 0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 1), c("0", "0 to 0.01", "0.01 to 0.02", "0.02 to 0.05", "0.05 to 0.1", "0.1 to 1")), mean))
```
