```{r}
#| label: landscape-structure
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# ETH global canopy height 2020 at 10 m and its standard deviation (Lang et al. 2023), Earth Engine users/nlang/ETH_GlobalCanopyHeight_2020_10m_v1 and ETH_GlobalCanopyHeightSD_2020_10m_v1.
# https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-023-02206-6 and https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/canopy/
# USGS 3D Elevation Program 10 m terrain, the Alaska 5 m interferometric radar terrain model resampled, Earth Engine USGS/3DEP/10m_collection.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/USGS_3DEP_10m_collection
# Copernicus GLO-30 surface model, Earth Engine COPERNICUS/DEM/GLO30_2024_1.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/COPERNICUS_DEM_GLO30_2024_1
# ArcticDEM version 4 surface model mosaic at 2 m, Earth Engine UMN/PGC/ArcticDEM/V4/2m_mosaic.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/UMN_PGC_ArcticDEM_V4_2m_mosaic
# JAXA ALOS PALSAR and PALSAR-2 yearly mosaics at 25 m, Earth Engine JAXA/ALOS/PALSAR/YEARLY/SAR.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/JAXA_ALOS_PALSAR_YEARLY_SAR
struct_tif <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_structure.tif"
if (!file.exists(struct_tif)) {
  at <- function(img, m) img$setDefaultProjection("EPSG:32605", NULL, m)$reduceResolution(ee$Reducer$mean(), maxPixels = 1024L)  # declare the source cell size, then average the cells inside each 90 m cell
  gamma0 <- function(img) img$select(c("HH", "HV"))$pow(2)$multiply(10^-8.3)$updateMask(img$select("qa")$eq(255))  # digital number to linear gamma0, 10 log10(DN^2) - 83 dB, land cells only
  lband <- function(y1, y2, e) ee$ImageCollection("JAXA/ALOS/PALSAR/YEARLY/SAR")$filterDate(paste0(y1, "-01-01"), paste0(y2, "-12-31"))$map(gamma0)$mean()$rename(paste0(c("HH", "HV"), "_", e))  # the years are filtered before the arithmetic, which drops the date stamp
  img <- ee$Image$cat(list(
    at(ee$Image("users/nlang/ETH_GlobalCanopyHeight_2020_10m_v1")$rename("eth"), 10), at(ee$Image("users/nlang/ETH_GlobalCanopyHeightSD_2020_10m_v1")$rename("eth_sd"), 10),
    at(ee$ImageCollection("USGS/3DEP/10m_collection")$mosaic()$select("elevation")$rename("dtm"), 10),
    at(ee$ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/DEM/GLO30_2024_1")$mosaic()$select("DEM")$rename("glo"), 30),
    at(ee$Image("UMN/PGC/ArcticDEM/V4/2m_mosaic")$select("elevation")$rename("arctic"), 10),
    at(lband(2015, 2016, "pre"), 25), at(lband(2019, 2020, "late"), 25)))
  e <- as.vector(terra::ext(sev)); rows <- split(seq_len(nrow(sev)), ceiling(seq_len(nrow(sev)) / 60))
  tile_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_tiles"; dir.create(tile_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (r in rows) { f <- file.path(tile_dir, sprintf("structure_%03d.tif", min(r))); if (file.exists(f)) next  # sixty rows per request, on the grid of the severity map
    url <- img$getDownloadURL(list(crs = "EPSG:32605", crs_transform = c(90, 0, e[1], 0, -90, e[4] - (min(r) - 1) * 90), dimensions = c(ncol(sev), length(r)), format = "GEO_TIFF", filePerBand = FALSE))
    for (attempt in 1:4) if (inherits(try(download.file(url, f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE), silent = TRUE), "try-error")) { unlink(f); Sys.sleep(30) } else break
    if (!file.exists(f)) stop("tile ", f, " did not download") }
  terra::writeRaster(terra::merge(terra::sprc(lapply(list.files(tile_dir, "^structure_.*\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE), terra::rast))), struct_tif) }
st <- terra::rast(struct_tif); names(st) <- c("eth", "eth_sd", "dtm", "glo", "arctic", "HH_pre", "HV_pre", "HH_late", "HV_late")
```

```{r}
#| label: structure-test
#| echo: true
#| output: false
sv <- as.data.frame(terra::values(st))[as.integer(rownames(land)), ]  # the same cells as `land`, which na.omit left numbered by cell
sv$arctic[!is.na(sv$arctic) & sv$arctic <= 0] <- NA  # the mosaic covers half the strip
land <- cbind(land, height_eth = sv$eth, height_eth_sd = sv$eth_sd, height_glo = sv$glo - sv$dtm, height_arctic = sv$arctic - sv$dtm,  # surface model minus terrain model, an offset-free canopy height
  HV_pre = 10 * log10(sv$HV_pre), HH_pre = 10 * log10(sv$HH_pre), HV_change = 10 * log10(sv$HV_late / sv$HV_pre))
auc_ok <- function(x, y) { ok <- !is.na(x); auc(x[ok], y[ok]) }
struct <- sapply(c("height_eth", "height_glo", "height_arctic", "HV_pre", "HH_pre", "HV_change", "VV65_pre", "VV131_pre"), function(v) { x <- land[[v]]; ok <- !is.na(x)
  c(n = sum(ok & lab_l), AUC = auc_ok(x[lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]), dead = mean(x[ok & lab_l & dead_l]), alive = mean(x[ok & lab_l & !dead_l]),
    rho_sev = cor(x[ok & forest_l], land$sev[ok & forest_l], method = "spearman"), rho_VV65 = cor(x[ok & forest_l], land$VV65_pre[ok & forest_l], method = "spearman"), rho_VV131 = cor(x[ok & forest_l], land$VV131_pre[ok & forest_l], method = "spearman")) })
d <- na.omit(data.frame(y = dead_l[lab_l], land[lab_l, c("height_eth", "height_glo", "HV_pre", "HH_pre", "VV65_pre", "VV131_pre")]))
fit_auc <- function(f) auc(predict(glm(f, family = binomial, data = d)), d$y)  # a logistic fit on the same cells, so the question is only whether a second source adds rank
added <- sapply(list(height = y ~ height_eth + height_glo, c_band = y ~ VV65_pre + VV131_pre, l_band = y ~ HV_pre + HH_pre, c_band_height = y ~ VV65_pre + VV131_pre + height_eth + height_glo, l_band_height = y ~ HV_pre + HH_pre + height_eth + height_glo, all = y ~ VV65_pre + VV131_pre + HV_pre + HH_pre + height_eth + height_glo), fit_auc)
struct_bins <- with(land[forest_l, ], sapply(list(height_eth = height_eth, height_glo = height_glo, HV_pre = HV_pre), function(x) tapply(x, cut(sev, c(-1, 0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 1), c("0", "0 to 0.01", "0.01 to 0.02", "0.02 to 0.05", "0.05 to 0.1", "0.1 to 1")), mean, na.rm = TRUE)))
write.csv(struct, "03.outputs/landscape_structure.csv")  # read by the abstract, which renders before this chunk
```

```{r}
#| label: landscape-landcover
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# LANDFIRE existing vegetation type version 1.4.0, Alaska, 30 m, Earth Engine LANDFIRE/Vegetation/EVT/v1_4_0, image AK, with its class legend in the image properties.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/LANDFIRE_Vegetation_EVT_v1_4_0
evt_tif <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_landfire.tif"; evt_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/landfire_evt_classes.csv"
if (!file.exists(evt_tif) || !file.exists(evt_csv)) {
  ak <- ee$ImageCollection("LANDFIRE/Vegetation/EVT/v1_4_0")$filter(ee$Filter$eq("system:index", "AK"))$first()
  p <- ak$getInfo()$properties; write.csv(data.frame(value = unlist(p$EVT_class_values), name = unlist(p$EVT_class_names)), evt_csv, row.names = FALSE)
  img <- ak$select("EVT")$setDefaultProjection("EPSG:32605", NULL, 30)$reduceResolution(ee$Reducer$mode(), maxPixels = 1024L)  # the commonest 30 m class inside each 90 m cell
  e <- as.vector(terra::ext(sev)); rows <- split(seq_len(nrow(sev)), ceiling(seq_len(nrow(sev)) / 60))
  tile_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_tiles"; dir.create(tile_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (r in rows) { f <- file.path(tile_dir, sprintf("landfire_%03d.tif", min(r))); if (file.exists(f)) next  # sixty rows per request, on the grid of the severity map
    url <- img$getDownloadURL(list(crs = "EPSG:32605", crs_transform = c(90, 0, e[1], 0, -90, e[4] - (min(r) - 1) * 90), dimensions = c(ncol(sev), length(r)), format = "GEO_TIFF", filePerBand = FALSE))
    for (attempt in 1:4) if (inherits(try(download.file(url, f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE), silent = TRUE), "try-error")) { unlink(f); Sys.sleep(30) } else break
    if (!file.exists(f)) stop("tile ", f, " did not download") }
  terra::writeRaster(terra::merge(terra::sprc(lapply(list.files(tile_dir, "^landfire_.*\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE), terra::rast))), evt_tif) }
evt_classes <- read.csv(evt_csv)
land$evt <- evt_classes$name[match(terra::values(terra::rast(evt_tif))[as.integer(rownames(land)), 1], evt_classes$value)]  # the same cells as `land`
```

```{r}
#| label: landcover-test
#| echo: true
#| output: false
cover <- t(sapply(split(which(lab_l), land$evt[lab_l]), function(i) { y <- dead_l[i]; big <- sum(y) >= 100 && sum(!y) >= 100  # dead and living cells by vegetation class, and whether height still ranks them inside one class
  c(dead = sum(y), living = sum(!y), height_dead = mean(land$height_eth[i][y], na.rm = TRUE), height_living = mean(land$height_eth[i][!y], na.rm = TRUE),
    AUC_height = if (big) auc_ok(land$height_eth[i], y) else NA, AUC_VV65 = if (big) auc_ok(land$VV65_pre[i], y) else NA, AUC_HV = if (big) auc_ok(land$HV_pre[i], y) else NA) }))
cover <- cover[order(-(cover[, "dead"] + cover[, "living"])), ]
dc <- na.omit(data.frame(y = dead_l[lab_l], cls = land$evt[lab_l], land[lab_l, c("height_eth", "VV65_pre")]))
cover_added <- sapply(list(class = y ~ cls, height = y ~ height_eth, class_height = y ~ cls + height_eth, class_c_band = y ~ cls + VV65_pre), function(f) auc(predict(glm(f, family = binomial, data = dc)), dc$y))  # does height add rank once the class is known
```

The stand validation covered `r nrow(stands)` stands chosen by @Zwieback_2024, so the pre-outbreak level was then scored across their whole severity map, a strip `r ncol(sev) * 90 / 1000` by `r round(nrow(sev) * 90 / 1000)` km mapped at 90 m from the WorldView-2 image of 2 August 2021. The mean slope-corrected VV of every scene of each orbit in October 2014 to December 2016 and in June 2019 to August 2021 was averaged into the 90 m cells of that map in Earth Engine. Of the `r format(nrow(land), big.mark = ",")` cells with values, a cell was dead at a severity of 0.01 or more and living at a severity of 0 with conifer top cover of 5 per cent or more, and the level, the change and Spearman's rank correlation with severity over every forest cell were computed as for the stands. The three canopy heights and the L-band mosaics of 2015 and 2016 were averaged into the same cells and scored the same way, and logistic regressions on the cells with every source present tested whether a second source added rank to the first. The survey polygons of 2017 to 2024 were rasterised onto the same cells so that the level could be scored against the survey as label on the same ground, and the LANDFIRE class of each cell tested whether the height contrast was a contrast between host and non-host cover or held within the classes.

## Statewide map

```{r}
#| label: statewide-angle
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Sentinel-1 GRD and the ETH canopy height 2020, read above; US Census TIGER/Line 2018 state boundaries, Earth Engine TIGER/2018/States (row `TIGER/2018/States` of 02.inputs/README.md).
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/TIGER_2018_States
angle_csv <- "03.outputs/statewide_angle.csv"
ak <- ee$FeatureCollection("TIGER/2018/States")$filter(ee$Filter$eq("NAME", "Alaska"))$geometry()
ak_box <- ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(-170, 54, -129, 71.5), "EPSG:4326", FALSE)  # the forested state without the far Aleutians, which cross the antimeridian
eth10 <- ee$Image("users/nlang/ETH_GlobalCanopyHeight_2020_10m_v1")$select(0)$rename("height")
forest10 <- eth10$gte(5)  # forest is a 10 m cell with canopy height of 5 m or more
s1_pre <- s1_all$filterBounds(ak)$filterDate("2014-10-01", "2017-01-01")  # every VV scene over Alaska from October 2014 to December 2016
if (!file.exists(angle_csv)) {  # how slope-corrected VV falls with incidence angle over forest, fitted inside each of 150 scenes drawn at random, so that scenes of every orbit can be pooled
  fits <- s1_pre$randomColumn("r", 20261014L)$sort("r")$limit(150L)$map(function(img) { img <- ee$Image(img)  # flatten names its one band "constant", so it is renamed before the fit
    ee$Feature(NULL, flatten(img, "VV")$rename("VV")$addBands(img$select("angle"))$updateMask(forest10)$select(list("angle", "VV"))$reduceRegion(ee$Reducer$linearFit(), img$geometry(), 300, maxPixels = 1e9, tileScale = 4))$set(list(orbit = img$get("relativeOrbitNumber_start"), date = img$date()$format("YYYY-MM-dd"))) })
  fits <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(fits$getInfo()$features, function(f) Filter(Negate(is.null), f$properties)))
  write.csv(data.frame(fits, slope_median = median(fits$scale, na.rm = TRUE)), angle_csv, row.names = FALSE) }
angle_fit <- read.csv(angle_csv); angle_slope <- angle_fit$slope_median[1]  # dB per degree of incidence angle
```

```{r}
#| label: statewide
#| echo: true
#| output: false
task_csv <- "03.outputs/statewide_task.csv"; asset_id <- paste0("projects/", ee_project, "/assets/spruce_susceptibility_alaska_90m")
norm_vv <- function(img) flatten(img, "VV", smooth = FALSE)$rename("VV")$subtract(img$select("angle")$subtract(38)$multiply(angle_slope))$rename("VV")  # slope-corrected VV brought to the mid-swath incidence angle of 38 degrees; the mean over scenes replaces the 3 by 3 filter
lin <- function(img) ee$Image$constant(10)$pow(img$divide(10))$rename("VV")  # decibels to linear power; the constant image names the result "constant" unless renamed
pre_vv <- s1_pre$map(norm_vv)
pooled_lin <- pre_vv$map(lin)$reduce(ee$Reducer$mean()$combine(ee$Reducer$count(), sharedInputs = TRUE))  # the mean of every scene in linear power and the scene count in one pass
pooled_s1 <- ee$Image$cat(list(pooled_lin$select("VV_mean")$log10()$multiply(10)$rename("VV"), pooled_lin$select("VV_count")$rename("scenes")))  # VV in decibels and the scene count, computed at whatever scale is requested, 90 m throughout this study, so each scene is read at the 90 m level of its image pyramid
at90 <- function(img, crs = "EPSG:3338") img$setDefaultProjection(crs, NULL, 10)$reduceResolution(ee$Reducer$mean(), maxPixels = 256L)  # the 10 m cells averaged into each 90 m cell
pooled_image <- function(crs = "EPSG:3338") { s <- at90(ee$Image$cat(list(eth10, forest10$unmask(0)$rename("forest"))), crs)  # canopy height as the cell mean and forest as the share of the cell, both from 10 m
  ee$Image$cat(list(pooled_s1, s))$updateMask(s$select("forest")$gt(0)) }
pooled <- pooled_image()
if (!file.exists(task_csv)) {  # the 90 m statewide map, exported once to an asset of the Earth Engine project, where the managers and the figure below read it
  task <- ee$batch$Export$image$toAsset(image = pooled$multiply(100)$round()$toInt16(), description = "spruce_susceptibility_alaska_90m", assetId = asset_id, region = ak_box, crs = "EPSG:3338", crsTransform = list(90, 0, 0, 0, -90, 0), maxPixels = 1e10, pyramidingPolicy = list(.default = "mean"), shardSize = 64L)  # a 64-cell shard reads a 576 by 576 window of 10 m cells; the default 256 exceeded the worker memory limit at 32 per cent on 2026-10-14
  task$start(); write.csv(data.frame(task = task$id, asset = asset_id, started = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")), task_csv, row.names = FALSE) }
```

```{r}
#| label: statewide-strip
#| echo: true
#| output: false
pooled_tif <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_s1_pooled.tif"
if (!file.exists(pooled_tif)) {  # the statewide product on the cells of the severity map, ten rows per request, so that the map is validated exactly as it is made
  img <- pooled_image("EPSG:32605"); e <- as.vector(terra::ext(sev)); rows <- split(seq_len(nrow(sev)), ceiling(seq_len(nrow(sev)) / 10))
  tile_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_tiles"; dir.create(tile_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (r in rows) { f <- file.path(tile_dir, sprintf("pooled_%03d.tif", min(r))); if (file.exists(f)) next
    for (attempt in 1:6) { ok <- !inherits(try({ url <- img$getDownloadURL(list(crs = "EPSG:32605", crs_transform = c(90, 0, e[1], 0, -90, e[4] - (min(r) - 1) * 90), dimensions = c(ncol(sev), length(r)), format = "GEO_TIFF", filePerBand = FALSE))
      download.file(url, f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE) }, silent = TRUE), "try-error"); if (ok) break; unlink(f); Sys.sleep(30) }  # the request itself times out under load now and then, so it is retried with the download
    if (!file.exists(f)) stop("tile ", f, " did not download") }
  terra::writeRaster(terra::merge(terra::sprc(lapply(list.files(tile_dir, "^pooled_.*\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE), terra::rast))), pooled_tif) }
pl <- terra::rast(pooled_tif); names(pl) <- c("VV_pooled", "scenes", "height_pooled", "forest")  # the GeoTIFF carries no band names
pv <- as.data.frame(terra::values(pl))[as.integer(rownames(land)), ]; land$VV_pooled <- pv$VV_pooled; land$scenes <- pv$scenes
youden <- function(x, y) { ok <- !is.na(x); x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]; th <- sort(unique(round(x, 2))); j <- sapply(th, function(t) mean(x[y] >= t) + mean(x[!y] < t) - 1); th[which.max(j)] }  # the threshold with the largest sum of the two correct rates
pooled_strip <- c(n = sum(lab_l & !is.na(land$VV_pooled)), AUC = auc_ok(land$VV_pooled[lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]), AUC_height = auc_ok(land$height_eth[lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]), AUC_survey = auc_ok(land$VV_pooled[forest_l], land$survey[forest_l] == 1),
  dead = mean(land$VV_pooled[lab_l & dead_l], na.rm = TRUE), alive = mean(land$VV_pooled[lab_l & !dead_l], na.rm = TRUE), scenes = median(land$scenes[forest_l], na.rm = TRUE), rho_height = cor(land$VV_pooled[forest_l], land$height_eth[forest_l], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
  thr_VV = youden(land$VV_pooled[lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]), thr_height = youden(land$height_eth[lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]))
pooled_strip["sens_VV"] <- mean(land$VV_pooled[lab_l & dead_l] >= pooled_strip["thr_VV"], na.rm = TRUE); pooled_strip["spec_VV"] <- mean(land$VV_pooled[lab_l & !dead_l] < pooled_strip["thr_VV"], na.rm = TRUE)  # the two correct rates at the threshold
write.csv(data.frame(t(pooled_strip)), "03.outputs/statewide_strip.csv", row.names = FALSE)  # read by the abstract, which renders before this chunk
```

Every Sentinel-1 scene with VV over Alaska from October 2014 to December 2016 was pooled into one map. Slope-corrected VV falls with incidence angle across a swath, so scenes of different orbits cannot be averaged until that fall is removed; the fall was fitted within each of 150 scenes drawn at random, as the slope of VV against incidence angle over forest cells at 300 m, and the median slope, `r sprintf("%.3f", angle_slope)` dB per degree over the `r sum(!is.na(angle_fit$scale))` scenes that held forest, brought every scene to the mid-swath angle of 38 degrees. Forest was a 10 m cell with an ETH canopy height of 5 m or more. The product was computed at 90 m on the Alaska Albers grid, each scene being read at the 90 m level of its image pyramid, corrected for slope with the 90 m terrain and averaged over scenes in linear power without the 3 by 3 filter, which the mean over scenes made unnecessary, with the scene count, the mean canopy height of the 10 m cells and the forest share of the 10 m cells as further bands, and cells with no forest were masked. A first version computed from the 10 m cells of every scene exceeded the memory of the export workers at a third of the state after 147 processor-hours and was abandoned. The map was exported to an asset of the Earth Engine project, where it is read by the figure below and is available to managers. The product was then validated exactly as made, by reading it on the cells of the severity map and scoring it against the dead and living cells, against the survey and against the ETH height. The threshold with the largest sum of the two correct rates on the severity map, `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["thr_VV"])` dB, defined a susceptible cell in everything that follows, and the same rule gave `r sprintf("%.1f", pooled_strip["thr_height"])` m on the height map.

## Regional validation

```{r}
#| label: matsu
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# US Census TIGER/Line 2018 county boundaries, Earth Engine TIGER/2018/Counties, GEOID 02170 the Matanuska-Susitna Borough (row `TIGER/2018/Counties` of 02.inputs/README.md).
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/TIGER_2018_Counties
# USFS Forest Health Protection aerial detection survey, Alaska Region 10, all years, the damage areas and the surveyed areas.
# https://www.fs.usda.gov/foresthealth/docs/IDS_Data_for_Download/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb.zip
# ABoVE conifer top cover 2020 (Macander and Nelson 2022), ORNL DAAC https://doi.org/10.3334/ORNLDAAC/2032, read above as `conifer`; it covers nine tenths of the borough.
# The height and radar sources are those of the landscape chunks above, ETH canopy height 2020, USGS 3DEP 10 m terrain, Copernicus GLO-30, ArcticDEM version 4, JAXA ALOS PALSAR yearly mosaics 2007 to 2010 and 2015 to 2016, and Sentinel-1 GRD.
gdb <- "02.inputs/ids-region10/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb"
predictor_image <- function(crs = "EPSG:3338") {  # the pre-outbreak height and radar sources of the strip, averaged into the 90 m cells of the given grid
  at3 <- function(img, m) img$setDefaultProjection(crs, NULL, m)$reduceResolution(ee$Reducer$mean(), maxPixels = 4096L)  # declare the source cell size, then average the cells inside each 90 m cell
  gamma0 <- function(img) img$select(c("HH", "HV"))$pow(2)$multiply(10^-8.3)$updateMask(img$select("qa")$eq(255))
  lband <- function(y1, y2, e) ee$ImageCollection("JAXA/ALOS/PALSAR/YEARLY/SAR")$filterDate(paste0(y1, "-01-01"), paste0(y2, "-12-31"))$map(gamma0)$mean()$rename(paste0(c("HH", "HV"), "_", e))
  vv_pre <- function(o) s1_all$filter(ee$Filter$eq("relativeOrbitNumber_start", o))$filterDate("2014-10-01", "2017-01-01")$map(function(img) flatten(img, "VV"))$mean()$rename(paste0("VV", o))  # the same era as the strip
  ee$Image$cat(list(at3(ee$Image("users/nlang/ETH_GlobalCanopyHeight_2020_10m_v1")$rename("eth"), 10), at3(ee$ImageCollection("USGS/3DEP/10m_collection")$mosaic()$select("elevation")$rename("dtm"), 10),
    at3(ee$ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/DEM/GLO30_2024_1")$mosaic()$select("DEM")$rename("glo"), 30), at3(ee$Image("UMN/PGC/ArcticDEM/V4/2m_mosaic")$select("elevation")$rename("arctic"), 10),
    at3(lband(2007, 2010, "2007"), 25), at3(lband(2015, 2016, "2015"), 25), at3(vv_pre(orbits[1]), 10), at3(vv_pre(orbits[2]), 10))) }
pull_cells <- function(smp, prefix, buffer = 0, crs = "EPSG:3338", img = predictor_image(crs)) {  # the 90 m cell of `img` holding each point, or the mean of the cells within `buffer` metres of it, a thousand points per request
  tile_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_tiles"; dir.create(tile_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (b in split(seq_len(nrow(smp)), ceiling(seq_len(nrow(smp)) / 1000))) { f <- file.path(tile_dir, sprintf("%s_%05d.csv", prefix, min(b))); if (file.exists(f)) next  # kept so that a failed run resumes
    pts <- ee$FeatureCollection(lapply(b, function(i) list(type = "Feature", geometry = list(type = "Point", coordinates = c(smp$lon[i], smp$lat[i])), properties = list(cell = smp$cell[i]))))
    if (buffer > 0) pts <- pts$map(function(ft) ee$Feature(ft)$buffer(buffer))
    for (attempt in 1:4) { z <- try(img$reduceRegions(collection = pts, reducer = if (buffer > 0) ee$Reducer$mean() else ee$Reducer$first(), scale = 90, crs = crs, tileScale = 16)$getInfo()$features, silent = TRUE); if (inherits(z, "try-error")) Sys.sleep(30) else break }
    if (inherits(z, "try-error")) stop("batch ", f, " did not return: ", z); write.csv(dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(z, function(q) Filter(Negate(is.null), q$properties))), f, row.names = FALSE) }
  got <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(list.files(tile_dir, sprintf("^%s_[0-9]+\\.csv$", prefix), full.names = TRUE), read.csv)); got[match(smp$cell, got$cell), setdiff(names(got), "cell")] }
region_sample <- function(geoids, csv, img = predictor_image(), prefix = paste0("region_", geoids[1]), n = 20000, reach = 10000, seed = 20261013) {  # one row per sampled 90 m cell of one or more boroughs, dead or living by the survey, with the bands of `img` read from Earth Engine
  if (file.exists(csv)) return(read.csv(csv))
  fc <- ee$FeatureCollection("TIGER/2018/Counties")$filter(ee$Filter$inList("GEOID", as.list(geoids))); tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson"); download.file(fc$getDownloadURL("geojson"), tmp, quiet = TRUE)
  bor <- sf::st_union(sf::st_transform(sf::st_read(tmp, quiet = TRUE), 3338)); e <- sf::st_bbox(bor)
  r <- terra::rast(terra::ext(floor(e$xmin / 90) * 90, ceiling(e$xmax / 90) * 90, floor(e$ymin / 90) * 90, ceiling(e$ymax / 90) * 90), resolution = 90, crs = "EPSG:3338")  # 90 m cells of the Alaska Albers grid with its origin at zero, the grid Earth Engine samples below
  sb <- sf::st_read(gdb, quiet = TRUE, query = "SELECT SURVEY_YEAR, HOST_CODE, PERCENT_MID, Shape FROM DAMAGE_AREAS_FLAT_AllYears_AK_Rgn10 WHERE DCA_CODE = 11009 AND SURVEY_YEAR >= 2014")
  sb <- sb[lengths(sf::st_intersects(sb, sf::st_as_sf(terra::as.polygons(terra::ext(r), crs = "EPSG:3338")))) > 0, ]; ws <- sb[sb$HOST_CODE == 94 & sb$SURVEY_YEAR %in% 2016:2024, ]  # spruce beetle on white spruce, 2016 to 2024
  year <- terra::setValues(r, NA_integer_); for (y in 2024:2016) year <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(ws[ws$SURVEY_YEAR == y, ]), year, field = y, update = TRUE)  # the first survey year in which a cell lay inside a white spruce polygon
  pct <- terra::setValues(r, 0); for (p in sort(unique(ws$PERCENT_MID))) pct <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(ws[ws$PERCENT_MID == p, ]), pct, field = p, update = TRUE)  # the highest mid-point of the polygon's mortality class over the years
  any_sb <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(sb), r, field = 1, background = 0)  # any spruce beetle polygon of any host or year, so a living cell was never marked
  fl <- sf::st_read(gdb, quiet = TRUE, query = "SELECT SURVEY_YEAR, Shape FROM SURVEYED_AREAS_FLAT_AllYears_AK_Rgn10 WHERE SURVEY_YEAR BETWEEN 2016 AND 2024")
  flown <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(fl), r, field = 1, background = 0)  # the ground the surveyors flew over in those years
  con <- terra::project(terra::crop(conifer, terra::project(terra::as.polygons(terra::ext(r), crs = "EPSG:3338"), terra::crs(conifer))), r, method = "average")
  inb <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(bor), r, field = 1, background = 0); strip <- terra::rasterize(terra::project(terra::as.polygons(terra::ext(sev), crs = "EPSG:32605"), "EPSG:3338"), r, field = 1, background = 0)
  ok <- which(terra::values(inb)[, 1] == 1 & terra::values(strip)[, 1] == 0 & terra::values(flown)[, 1] == 1 & terra::values(con)[, 1] >= 5)  # conifer top cover of 5 per cent or more, flown, inside the borough and outside the severity strip
  v <- data.frame(cell = ok, year = terra::values(year)[ok, 1], pct = terra::values(pct)[ok, 1], marked = terra::values(any_sb)[ok, 1], conifer = terra::values(con)[ok, 1])
  set.seed(seed); dead <- v[sample(which(!is.na(v$year)), min(n, sum(!is.na(v$year)))), ]; dead$dist <- 0
  living <- v[sample(which(v$marked == 0), min(4 * n, sum(v$marked == 0))), ]  # drawn four times over, then kept only within reach of a white spruce polygon
  pts <- sf::st_as_sf(data.frame(terra::xyFromCell(r, living$cell)), coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3338)
  living$dist <- as.numeric(sf::st_distance(pts, ws[sf::st_nearest_feature(pts, ws), ], by_element = TRUE)); living <- head(living[living$dist <= reach, ], n)
  smp <- rbind(dead, living); smp[, c("x", "y")] <- terra::xyFromCell(r, smp$cell); ll <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(smp, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3338), 4326)); smp$lon <- ll[, 1]; smp$lat <- ll[, 2]; smp <- smp[order(round(smp$x / 20000), smp$y), ]  # sorted into 20 km columns, so that one request touches few image tiles
  smp <- cbind(smp, pull_cells(smp, prefix, img = img)); write.csv(smp, csv, row.names = FALSE); smp }
ms <- region_sample("02170", "02.inputs/derived/matsu_sample.csv")
```

```{r}
#| label: matsu-test
#| echo: true
#| output: false
ms$dead <- !is.na(ms$year); ms$arctic[!is.na(ms$arctic) & ms$arctic <= 0] <- NA
ms <- cbind(ms, height_eth = ms$eth, height_glo = ms$glo - ms$dtm, height_arctic = ms$arctic - ms$dtm, HV_2007 = 10 * log10(ms$HV_2007), HH_2007 = 10 * log10(ms$HH_2007), HV_2015 = 10 * log10(ms$HV_2015), HH_2015 = 10 * log10(ms$HH_2015))[, -match(c("HV_2007", "HH_2007", "HV_2015", "HH_2015"), names(ms))]
ms_vars <- c("height_eth", "height_glo", "height_arctic", "HV_2007", "HH_2007", "HV_2015", "HH_2015", "VV65", "VV131")
ms_names <- c(height_eth = "ETH canopy height", height_glo = "the GLO-30 surface minus terrain", height_arctic = "the ArcticDEM surface minus terrain", HV_2007 = "L-band HV of 2007 to 2010", HH_2007 = "L-band HH of 2007 to 2010", HV_2015 = "L-band HV of 2015 and 2016", HH_2015 = "L-band HH of 2015 and 2016", VV65 = "the ascending C-band level", VV131 = "the descending C-band level")  # the sources as the text names them
matsu <- sapply(ms_vars, function(v) { x <- ms[[v]]; ok <- !is.na(x); sev_ok <- ok & (ms$pct >= 20 | !ms$dead); edge <- ok & (ms$dead | ms$dist >= 500)  # every cell, then only the polygons of a fifth or more mortality, then only the living cells at least 500 m from a polygon edge
  c(n = sum(ok), AUC = auc_ok(x, ms$dead), AUC_severe = auc(x[sev_ok], ms$dead[sev_ok]), AUC_edge = auc(x[edge], ms$dead[edge]), dead = mean(x[ok & ms$dead]), living = mean(x[ok & !ms$dead]), rho_pct = cor(x[ok], ms$pct[ok], method = "spearman")) })
dm <- na.omit(ms[, c("dead", "height_eth", "height_glo", "HV_2007", "HH_2007", "VV65", "VV131")])
ms_added <- sapply(list(height = dead ~ height_eth + height_glo, c_band = dead ~ VV65 + VV131, l_band = dead ~ HV_2007 + HH_2007, c_band_height = dead ~ VV65 + VV131 + height_eth + height_glo, l_band_height = dead ~ HV_2007 + HH_2007 + height_eth + height_glo, all = dead ~ VV65 + VV131 + HV_2007 + HH_2007 + height_eth + height_glo),
  function(f) auc(predict(glm(f, family = binomial, data = dm)), dm$dead))  # the same six fits as the strip, on the cells with every source
ms_year <- with(ms[ms$dead, ], sapply(list(height_eth = height_eth, height_glo = height_glo, height_arctic = height_arctic, HV_2007 = HV_2007), function(x) tapply(x, year, mean, na.rm = TRUE)))  # the stands first attacked in each year, by their height before the outbreak
ms_year_n <- table(ms$year[ms$dead]); ms_trend <- with(ms[ms$dead, ], sapply(list(height_eth = height_eth, height_glo = height_glo, height_arctic = height_arctic, HV_2007 = HV_2007), function(x) cor(x, year, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")))

names(pooled_region) <- names(regions)
region_auc <- sapply(pooled_region, function(s) { s$dead <- !is.na(s$year)
  c(dead = sum(s$dead), living = sum(!s$dead), AUC_VV = auc_ok(s$VV, s$dead), AUC_height = auc_ok(s$height, s$dead), VV_dead = mean(s$VV[s$dead], na.rm = TRUE), VV_living = mean(s$VV[!s$dead], na.rm = TRUE), height_dead = mean(s$height[s$dead], na.rm = TRUE), height_living = mean(s$height[!s$dead], na.rm = TRUE),
    above_dead = mean(s$VV[s$dead] >= pooled_strip["thr_VV"], na.rm = TRUE), above_living = mean(s$VV[!s$dead] >= pooled_strip["thr_VV"], na.rm = TRUE),  # the share of each class the strip's threshold calls susceptible
    rho_year_height = if (sum(s$dead) >= 30) cor(s$height[s$dead], s$year[s$dead], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs") else NA, years = length(unique(s$year[s$dead]))) })
write.csv(region_auc, "03.outputs/statewide_regions.csv")  # read by the abstract, which renders before this chunk
```

The map was tested against the aerial detection survey, the only label beyond the strip, in the four regions of @fig-study, three in which the outbreak has run for years and one, the Interior, at its northern front. In each region a 90 m grid was laid on the Alaska Albers projection, and the survey's spruce beetle polygons on white spruce from 2016 to 2024 gave each cell its first year inside a polygon and the highest mortality class recorded over it. A cell was dead if it lay inside such a polygon and held conifer top cover of 5 per cent or more. A cell was living if it held that cover, lay inside the ground the surveyors flew over in those years, had never lain inside a spruce beetle polygon of any host or year, and lay within 10 km of a white spruce polygon, so that the living class held forest the beetle could have reached and the surveyors had looked at. The cells of the severity map were excluded. Of the eligible cells, 5,000 dead and 5,000 living were drawn at random with a fixed seed in each region, or every cell where fewer existed, and the statewide product was read at them in Earth Engine. Each region was scored by the area under the curve for dead against living, by the share of each class the strip's threshold called susceptible, and by Spearman's rank correlation between the year a dead cell was first recorded and its canopy height, to test whether the beetle moved from taller to shorter stands as the outbreak proceeded, as @Hard_1985 and @Werner_1983 reported for the Kenai. In the Matanuska-Susitna Borough the nine single-orbit and height sources of the strip were also read at `r format(sum(ms$dead), big.mark = ",")` dead and `r format(sum(!ms$dead), big.mark = ",")` living cells drawn the same way, the PALSAR mosaics of 2007 to 2010 being added because they predate every damage polygon, so that the ceiling the survey label sets on any source could be measured.

## Ground plots

```{r}
#| label: fia
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# USFS Forest Inventory and Analysis DataMart, Alaska PLOT and TREE tables as CSV, plot coordinates published fuzzed by up to about a mile (row `fia-alaska/` of 02.inputs/README.md).
# https://apps.fs.usda.gov/fia/datamart/CSV/AK_PLOT.zip and https://apps.fs.usda.gov/fia/datamart/CSV/AK_TREE.zip
fia_dir <- "02.inputs/fia-alaska"; dir.create(fia_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
for (t in c("PLOT", "TREE")) if (!file.exists(file.path(fia_dir, paste0("AK_", t, ".csv")))) { z <- file.path(fia_dir, paste0("AK_", t, ".zip")); options(timeout = 600)
  download.file(paste0("https://apps.fs.usda.gov/fia/datamart/CSV/AK_", t, ".zip"), z, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE); unzip(z, exdir = fia_dir); unlink(z) }
fia_region <- function(counties, csv) {  # one row per forested plot of the named boroughs at its latest measurement, the white spruce tallied on it, and the satellite height at its published coordinate
  if (file.exists(csv)) return(read.csv(csv, colClasses = c(CN = "character")))
  pl <- read.csv(file.path(fia_dir, "AK_PLOT.csv"), colClasses = c(CN = "character")); pl <- pl[pl$COUNTYCD %in% counties & pl$PLOT_STATUS_CD == 1, ]
  pl <- pl[order(-pl$MEASYEAR), ]; pl <- pl[!duplicated(paste(pl$COUNTYCD, pl$PLOT)), ]  # a remeasured plot enters once, at its latest visit
  tr <- read.csv(file.path(fia_dir, "AK_TREE.csv"), colClasses = c(PLT_CN = "character")); ws <- tr[tr$PLT_CN %in% pl$CN & tr$SPCD == 94 & tr$STATUSCD %in% 1:2 & !is.na(tr$DIA), ]  # every live or standing dead white spruce tallied with a diameter; the Kenai remeasurements carry 699 dead trees tallied without one
  ba <- function(d, tpa) sum(pi * (d * 0.0127)^2 * tpa * 2.471, na.rm = TRUE)  # basal area in square metres per hectare from diameter in inches and trees per acre
  f <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ws, ws$PLT_CN), function(w) { dd <- w$STATUSCD == 2; data.frame(CN = w$PLT_CN[1], n_ws = nrow(w), n_dead = sum(dd), ba_ws = ba(w$DIA, w$TPA_UNADJ), dead_share = ba(w$DIA[dd], w$TPA_UNADJ[dd]) / ba(w$DIA, w$TPA_UNADJ),
    ht_live = mean(w$HT[!dd]) * 0.3048, ht_dead = mean(w$HT[dd]) * 0.3048, ht_max = max(w$HT) * 0.3048, dia_live = mean(w$DIA[!dd]) * 2.54, dia_dead = mean(w$DIA[dd]) * 2.54,
    beetle = sum(!dd & (w$DAMAGE_AGENT_CD1 %in% 11009 | w$DAMAGE_AGENT_CD2 %in% 11009 | w$DAMAGE_AGENT_CD3 %in% 11009)), recent = sum(dd & w$DECAYCD %in% 1:2)) }))  # live trees carrying the survey's spruce beetle code 11009, and dead trees still holding their bark and fine branches
  f <- cbind(f, pl[match(f$CN, pl$CN), c("MEASYEAR", "LAT", "LON")]); names(f)[match(c("LAT", "LON"), names(f))] <- c("lat", "lon"); f$cell <- seq_len(nrow(f))
  near <- pull_cells(f, paste0("fia_cell_", counties[1])); wide <- pull_cells(f, paste0("fia_800m_", counties[1]), buffer = 800); names(wide) <- paste0(names(wide), "_800m")  # the 90 m cell at the published coordinate, and the mean of the cells within 800 m of it, the fuzzing distance
  f <- cbind(f, near, wide); write.csv(f, csv, row.names = FALSE); f }
fia_regions <- list(matsu = fia_region(170, "02.inputs/derived/fia_matsu.csv"), kenai = fia_region(122, "02.inputs/derived/fia_kenai.csv"),  # Matanuska-Susitna and Kenai Peninsula boroughs
  copper = fia_region(261, "02.inputs/derived/fia_copper.csv"), interior = fia_region(c(68, 90, 240, 290), "02.inputs/derived/fia_interior.csv"))  # Valdez-Cordova, and Denali, Fairbanks North Star, Southeast Fairbanks and Yukon-Koyukuk of the Interior, measured in 2014 to 2019 before the outbreak's front entered the Denali Borough
```

```{r}
#| label: fia-test
#| echo: true
#| output: false
fia_regions <- lapply(fia_regions, function(f) { for (s in c("", "_800m")) { f[[paste0("height_glo", s)]] <- f[[paste0("glo", s)]] - f[[paste0("dtm", s)]]; f[[paste0("HV_2007", s)]] <- 10 * log10(f[[paste0("HV_2007", s)]]) }; f })
fia_ground <- sapply(fia_regions, function(f) { b <- f[f$n_dead > 0 & f$n_dead < f$n_ws, ]  # the plots holding both live and dead white spruce
  c(plots = nrow(f), from = min(f$MEASYEAR), to = max(f$MEASYEAR), both = nrow(b), dia_dead = mean(b$dia_dead), dia_live = mean(b$dia_live), ht_dead = mean(b$ht_dead), ht_live = mean(b$ht_live),
    V_dia = unname(wilcox.test(b$dia_dead, b$dia_live, paired = TRUE)$statistic), p_dia = wilcox.test(b$dia_dead, b$dia_live, paired = TRUE)$p.value,  # within one plot, were the trees that died the larger ones
    V_ht = unname(wilcox.test(b$ht_dead, b$ht_live, paired = TRUE)$statistic), p_ht = wilcox.test(b$ht_dead, b$ht_live, paired = TRUE)$p.value,
    dead_share = mean(f$dead_share), half_dead = sum(f$dead_share >= 0.5), beetle_plots = sum(f$beetle > 0), recent = sum(f$recent) / sum(f$n_dead),
    rho_share_ht = cor(f$dead_share, f$ht_max, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"), AUC_ht_half = auc_ok(f$ht_max, f$dead_share >= 0.5)) })  # across plots, did the taller white spruce stands lose the larger share
sat <- function(f, v, s = "_800m") { x <- f[[paste0(v, s)]]; ok <- !is.na(x); if (sum(ok) < 30) return(c(n = sum(ok), rho_ht = NA, AUC_half = NA))
  c(n = sum(ok), rho_ht = cor(x[ok], f$ht_max[ok], method = "spearman"), AUC_half = auc(x[ok], f$dead_share[ok] >= 0.5)) }  # the satellite height around the published coordinate against the plot's own tallest tree and its dead share
fia_remote <- sapply(fia_regions, function(f) unlist(lapply(c(eth = "eth", height_glo = "height_glo", HV_2007 = "HV_2007", VV65 = "VV65"), function(v) sat(f, v))))
fia_fuzz <- sapply(c(eth = "eth", height_glo = "height_glo", HV_2007 = "HV_2007", VV65 = "VV65"), function(v) c(cell = sat(fia_regions$matsu, v, "")[["AUC_half"]], m800 = sat(fia_regions$matsu, v)[["AUC_half"]]))  # the Mat-Su cell at the coordinate against the 800 m mean
pfmt <- function(p) if (p < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else sprintf("p = %.3f", p)  # the p-value as the text prints it
write.csv(fia_ground, "03.outputs/fia_ground.csv")  # read by the abstract, which renders before this chunk
```

The finding was checked on the ground against the public Forest Inventory and Analysis plots of Alaska [@Bechtold_2005]. Every forested plot of four regions was taken at its latest measurement, the Matanuska-Susitna Borough (`r fia_ground["plots", "matsu"]` plots with white spruce, measured `r fia_ground["from", "matsu"]` to `r fia_ground["to", "matsu"]`), the Kenai Peninsula Borough (`r fia_ground["plots", "kenai"]`, `r fia_ground["from", "kenai"]` to `r fia_ground["to", "kenai"]`), the Valdez-Cordova census area (`r fia_ground["plots", "copper"]`, `r fia_ground["from", "copper"]` to `r fia_ground["to", "copper"]`), and the Denali, Fairbanks North Star, Southeast Fairbanks and Yukon-Koyukuk areas of the Interior (`r fia_ground["plots", "interior"]`, `r fia_ground["from", "interior"]` to `r fia_ground["to", "interior"]`), measured before the outbreak's front entered the Denali Borough, so that the Interior plots stood for white spruce the beetle had not reached. For every live or standing dead white spruce on each plot the inventory records diameter, height and, for dead trees, a decay class, but no cause or year of death. On the plots holding both live and dead white spruce the mean diameter and height of the dead trees were set against those of the live trees with a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and across all plots the share of basal area dead was correlated with the height of the tallest tree, which also ranked the plots with at least half their basal area dead by the area under the curve. The satellite sources were read at each plot's published coordinate, which the inventory shifts by up to about a mile, both for the 90 m cell holding it and as the mean of the cells within 800 m.

# Results

## Literature

The searches returned `r format(review_counts["retrieved"], big.mark = ",")` records, `r review_counts["unique"]` of them unique after the strands were joined and `r review_counts["chased"]` more from the citation chase, of which `r review_counts["included"]` were retained and `r review_counts["excluded"]` excluded, most for bearing on neither question (`r review_reasons$records[review_reasons$reason == "wrong-concept"]`) or for another bark beetle (`r review_reasons$records[review_reasons$reason == "wrong-population"]`). Every retained study that measured which trees died found the larger and taller spruce dead first, from Colorado in the 1940s to the Copper River basin in the 2000s, and every hazard rating in the corpus rested on a cruise (@tbl-attributes). No retained record had mapped the susceptible stands of a region from satellite structure data, and none had scored Sentinel-1 or satellite canopy height against spruce beetle mortality on areas held out whole.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-attributes
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "The tree and stand attributes the review established as predictors of spruce beetle attack, the direction each is expected to take in a susceptibility map, and the records the expectation rests on."
attr_tbl <- read.csv("04.references/review/attributes.csv", check.names = FALSE)
fmt_tbl(setNames(attr_tbl, c("Attribute", "Expected direction", "Reasoning", "Sources")))
```

## Stand validation

At the 90 m stand scale, on `r sum(sacc$dead[sacc$design == "VV_2014" & sacc$set == "training"], sacc$alive[sacc$design == "VV_2014" & sacc$set == "training"])` training stands labelled dead (`r sacc$dead[sacc$design == "VV_2014" & sacc$set == "training"]`) or living forest (`r sacc$alive[sacc$design == "VV_2014" & sacc$set == "training"]`), the mean VV level of October 2014 to December 2016, before the outbreak reached the areas, ranked the stands the outbreak would kill above the living stands with an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", change$auc_pre[change$band == "VV131"])` on the descending orbit and `r sprintf("%.2f", change$auc_pre[change$band == "VV65"])` on the ascending, the dead stands being `r sprintf("%.1f", with(chg[chg$labelled & chg$band == "VV131", ], mean(pre[dead]) - mean(pre[!dead])))` dB brighter (@tbl-validation). The change from that level to June 2019 to August 2021 separated nothing, an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", change$auc_change[change$band == "VV131"])` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(change$auc_change))`, the dead stands changing by `r sprintf("%.2f", change$change_dead[change$band == "VV131"])` dB against `r sprintf("%.2f", change$change_alive[change$band == "VV131"])` dB for the living [Welch t-test, t(`r sprintf("%.0f", change$df[change$band == "VV131"])`) = `r sprintf("%.2f", change$t[change$band == "VV131"])`, `r pfmt(change$p[change$band == "VV131"])`], and conifer cover alone gave `r sprintf("%.2f", change$auc_conifer[1])`, so the pre-outbreak brightness was not canopy density. The network trained on the full monthly series reached an F1 score of `r sprintf("%.2f", sacc$F1[sacc$design == "VV_2014" & sacc$set == "training"])` and an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", sacc$AUC[sacc$design == "VV_2014" & sacc$set == "training"])` on held-out folds, and the untrained mean of one band matched it at `r sprintf("%.2f", max(unlist(sbase)))`, so the level alone was carried forward.

The crown labels are the 90 m stand cells of the Zwieback et al. (2024) training areas, the severity map their 90 m map of 2021, and the survey the aerial detection survey polygons of 2016 to 2024 across the rest of the Matanuska-Susitna Borough. The statewide product is the pooled, angle-corrected VV level of every scene; the two orbits are the single-orbit levels of the same months."

## Landscape validation

Across the `r format(nrow(land), big.mark = ",")` cells of the severity map, `r format(sum(dead_l[lab_l]), big.mark = ",")` dead and `r format(sum(!dead_l[lab_l]), big.mark = ",")` living forest, the pre-outbreak VV level ranked dead above living with an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", land_auc["level", "VV65"])` on the ascending orbit and `r sprintf("%.2f", land_auc["level", "VV131"])` on the descending, its rank correlation with severity over every forest cell was `r sprintf("%.2f", land_auc["rho", "VV65"])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", land_auc["rho", "VV131"])`, and the mean level rose with every severity bin from `r sprintf("%.2f", land_bins["0"])` dB at zero to `r sprintf("%.2f", land_bins["0.1 to 1"])` dB at 0.1 or more on the descending orbit, while the change gave `r sprintf("%.2f", land_auc["change", "VV65"])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", land_auc["change", "VV131"])`. The three canopy heights ranked the cells as well as the radar did. ETH canopy height gave `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["AUC", "height_eth"])`, with dead cells at `r sprintf("%.1f", struct["dead", "height_eth"])` m against living at `r sprintf("%.1f", struct["alive", "height_eth"])` m, the GLO-30 surface minus terrain `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["AUC", "height_glo"])` and the ArcticDEM surface minus terrain `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["AUC", "height_arctic"])`, L-band HV of 2015 and 2016 gave `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["AUC", "HV_pre"])`, and height and the C-band level were correlated over the forest cells [Spearman's rho `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["rho_VV65", "height_eth"])`]. On the `r format(nrow(d), big.mark = ",")` cells with every source, logistic fits gave `r sprintf("%.3f", added["height"])` for height alone, `r sprintf("%.3f", added["c_band"])` for C-band alone and `r sprintf("%.3f", added["all"])` for all three together. The contrast held inside the vegetation classes, in that within every LANDFIRE class with at least 100 cells of each kind height ranked dead above living, from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(cover[, "AUC_height"], na.rm = TRUE))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(cover[, "AUC_height"], na.rm = TRUE))`, and in Alaska Sub-boreal White Spruce Forest, the one white spruce class with enough cells, height gave `r sprintf("%.2f", cover["Alaska Sub-boreal White Spruce Forest", "AUC_height"])` with dead cells at `r sprintf("%.1f", cover["Alaska Sub-boreal White Spruce Forest", "height_dead"])` m against `r sprintf("%.1f", cover["Alaska Sub-boreal White Spruce Forest", "height_living"])` m, while logistic fits gave `r sprintf("%.3f", cover_added["class"])` for the class alone and `r sprintf("%.3f", cover_added["class_height"])` for class and height together.

## Statewide map

```{r}
#| label: statewide-map
#| echo: true
#| output: false
state_tif <- "02.inputs/derived/statewide_1km.tif"
if (!file.exists(state_tif)) {  # the exported asset read back at 1 km for the figure and the area table, once the export has finished
  task <- read.csv(task_csv)
  repeat { st <- ee$data$getTaskStatus(task$task)[[1]]$state; if (st == "COMPLETED") break; if (st %in% c("FAILED", "CANCELLED")) stop("export ", st); Sys.sleep(120) }
  a90 <- ee$Image(asset_id)$divide(100)  # the asset is masked where the 90 m cell holds no forest, so VV, scenes and height average over forest cells and the forest share is unmasked to zero before it is averaged, or the share would run high
  img <- ee$Image$cat(list(a90$select(list("VV", "scenes", "height")), a90$select("forest")$unmask(0)))$reduceResolution(ee$Reducer$mean(), maxPixels = 256L)  # 90 m cells averaged into each 1 km cell
  b <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = -170, ymin = 54, xmax = -129, ymax = 71.5), crs = 4326)), 3338)); x0 <- floor(b$xmin / 1000) * 1000; y1 <- ceiling(b$ymax / 1000) * 1000
  nc <- ceiling((b$xmax - x0) / 1000); nr <- ceiling((y1 - b$ymin) / 1000); rows <- split(seq_len(nr), ceiling(seq_len(nr) / 500))
  tile_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_tiles"
  for (r in rows) { f <- file.path(tile_dir, sprintf("state_%04d.tif", min(r))); if (file.exists(f)) next
    for (attempt in 1:6) { ok <- !inherits(try({ url <- img$getDownloadURL(list(crs = "EPSG:3338", crs_transform = c(1000, 0, x0, 0, -1000, y1 - (min(r) - 1) * 1000), dimensions = c(nc, length(r)), format = "GEO_TIFF", filePerBand = FALSE))
      download.file(url, f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE) }, silent = TRUE), "try-error"); if (ok) break; unlink(f); Sys.sleep(30) }
    if (!file.exists(f)) stop("tile ", f, " did not download") }
  terra::writeRaster(terra::merge(terra::sprc(lapply(list.files(tile_dir, "^state_.*\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE), terra::rast))), state_tif) }
alaska_geojson <- "02.inputs/context/alaska_tiger2018.geojson"  # the full-resolution state polygon, for clipping; the 1:20,000,000 outline above is for drawing
if (!file.exists(alaska_geojson)) download.file(ee$FeatureCollection("TIGER/2018/States")$filter(ee$Filter$eq("NAME", "Alaska"))$getDownloadURL("geojson"), alaska_geojson, quiet = TRUE)
state <- terra::mask(terra::rast(state_tif), terra::vect(sf::st_transform(sf::st_read(alaska_geojson, quiet = TRUE), 3338))); names(state) <- c("VV", "scenes", "height", "forest")  # the export rectangle runs east of the border, where the scene search returned nothing, so the map is clipped to the state
vv <- state$VV; vv[state$scenes == 0] <- NA; state$VV <- vv  # a cell no scene covered carries no level
state_area <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(names(regions), "alaska"), function(nm) {  # square kilometres of forest and of susceptible forest, the forest share of each 1 km cell summed
  v <- if (nm == "alaska") as.data.frame(terra::values(state)) else terra::extract(state, terra::vect(reg_sf[reg_sf$region == nm, ]), ID = FALSE)
  v <- v[!is.na(v$forest) & v$forest > 0, ]
  data.frame(region = nm, forest_km2 = sum(v$forest), susceptible_km2 = sum(v$forest[!is.na(v$VV) & v$VV >= pooled_strip["thr_VV"]]), tall_km2 = sum(v$forest[!is.na(v$height) & v$height >= pooled_strip["thr_height"]]), scenes = median(v$scenes, na.rm = TRUE)) }))
write.csv(state_area, "03.outputs/statewide_area.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-statewide
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: "The statewide susceptibility map at 1 km, the mean of the 90 m product over the forest cells of each 1 km cell. Left, the slope-corrected Sentinel-1 VV level of October 2014 to December 2016 brought to a 38 degree incidence angle; right, the ETH canopy height of 2020. Cells with less than a fifth of their area in forest are blank. Black outlines are the four test regions and the blue frame the validation strip."
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 3.9
forest_ok <- state$forest >= 0.2
pan <- function(layer, name, pal, lim) ggplot() + geom_sf(data = alaska, fill = "grey95", colour = NA) + tidyterra::geom_spatraster(data = terra::mask(state[[layer]], forest_ok, maskvalues = FALSE)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name, option = pal, limits = lim, oob = scales::squish, na.value = NA) + geom_sf(data = reg_sf, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3) + geom_sf(data = frame, fill = NA, colour = "#1F618D", linewidth = 0.6) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-1.55e6, 1.45e6), ylim = c(4.2e5, 2.35e6)) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + th + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = grid::unit(1.2, "cm"), legend.text = element_text(size = 7), legend.title = element_text(size = 8), axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())
pan("VV", "VV (dB)", "magma", c(-12, -6)) + pan("height", "Canopy height (m)", "viridis", c(5, 30))
```

The pooled product, read on the `r format(pooled_strip["n"], big.mark = ",")` labelled cells of the severity map, ranked dead above living with an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["AUC"])`, dead cells at `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["dead"])` dB against `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["alive"])` dB, from a median of `r pooled_strip["scenes"]` scenes per cell, and its rank correlation with ETH height over the forest cells was `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["rho_height"])`. At the threshold of `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["thr_VV"])` dB it called `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * pooled_strip["sens_VV"])` per cent of the dead cells and `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (1 - pooled_strip["spec_VV"]))` per cent of the living cells susceptible, and against the survey polygons on the same cells it gave `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["AUC_survey"])`. Across Alaska (@fig-statewide), `r format(round(state_area$forest_km2[state_area$region == "alaska"]), big.mark = ",")` km² of forest carried the map, `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * state_area$susceptible_km2[state_area$region == "alaska"] / state_area$forest_km2[state_area$region == "alaska"])` per cent of it at or above the threshold, and the share ran from `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * min(with(state_area[state_area$region != "alaska", ], susceptible_km2 / forest_km2)))` per cent in the `r region_names[state_area$region[state_area$region != "alaska"]][which.min(with(state_area[state_area$region != "alaska", ], susceptible_km2 / forest_km2))]` region to `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * max(with(state_area[state_area$region != "alaska", ], susceptible_km2 / forest_km2)))` per cent in the `r region_names[state_area$region[state_area$region != "alaska"]][which.max(with(state_area[state_area$region != "alaska", ], susceptible_km2 / forest_km2))]` region (@tbl-area).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-area
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "Forest and susceptible forest in the four test regions and in Alaska, from the 1 km map. Forest is the area of 10 m cells with canopy height of 5 m or more; susceptible forest is the forest whose pre-outbreak VV level reached the strip's threshold, and tall forest the forest whose canopy height reached the strip's height threshold. Scenes is the median number of Sentinel-1 scenes behind a forest cell."
fmt_tbl(data.frame(Region = c(region_names[state_area$region[state_area$region != "alaska"]], "Alaska"), `Forest (km²)` = format(round(state_area$forest_km2), big.mark = ","), `Susceptible (km²)` = format(round(state_area$susceptible_km2), big.mark = ","),
  `Susceptible (%)` = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * state_area$susceptible_km2 / state_area$forest_km2), `Tall (km²)` = format(round(state_area$tall_km2), big.mark = ","), Scenes = round(state_area$scenes), check.names = FALSE))
```

## Regional validation

Against the aerial detection survey the radar map ranked attacked above unattacked forest with an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", "kenai"])` on the Kenai Peninsula and `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", "matsu"])` in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, where the attacked stands were `r sprintf("%.1f", region_auc["VV_dead", "matsu"] - region_auc["VV_living", "matsu"])` dB brighter and `r sprintf("%.1f", region_auc["height_dead", "matsu"] - region_auc["height_living", "matsu"])` m taller than the unattacked, but not in the Copper River basin, `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", "copper"])`, where both classes were darker (`r sprintf("%.1f", region_auc["VV_dead", "copper"])` against `r sprintf("%.1f", region_auc["VV_living", "copper"])` dB) and shorter (`r sprintf("%.1f", region_auc["height_dead", "copper"])` against `r sprintf("%.1f", region_auc["height_living", "copper"])` m) than in the two southern regions and the survey had recorded damage only since 2022, and it gave `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", "interior"])` in the Interior, where the `r format(region_auc["dead", "interior"], big.mark = ",")` dead cells of the sample all lay between `r sprintf("%.1f", min(pooled_region$interior$lat[!is.na(pooled_region$interior$year)]))`° N and `r sprintf("%.1f", max(pooled_region$interior$lat[!is.na(pooled_region$interior$year)]))`° N along the Nenana River and `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * mean(pooled_region$interior$year[!is.na(pooled_region$interior$year)] >= 2021))` per cent of them were first recorded in 2021 or later. The height map gave `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_height", "kenai"])`, `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_height", "matsu"])`, `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_height", "copper"])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_height", "interior"])` (@tbl-regions). In the Matanuska-Susitna Borough the nine single sources scored from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(matsu["AUC", ]))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(matsu["AUC", ]))` against the same label, the highest being `r ms_names[colnames(matsu)[which.max(matsu["AUC", ])]]`, and limiting the dead cells to polygons of 20 per cent mortality or more changed nothing, `r sprintf("%.2f", min(matsu["AUC_severe", ]))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(matsu["AUC_severe", ]))`, so the survey label set the ceiling. The stands the survey first recorded in 2016 and 2017 were the tallest, `r sprintf("%.1f", ms_year["2016", "height_eth"])` and `r sprintf("%.1f", ms_year["2017", "height_eth"])` m on ETH height, and those first recorded in 2024 the shortest, `r sprintf("%.1f", ms_year["2024", "height_eth"])` m, with Spearman's rho between year and height of `r sprintf("%.2f", ms_trend["height_eth"])` over cohorts of `r format(min(ms_year_n), big.mark = ",")` to `r format(max(ms_year_n), big.mark = ",")` cells.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-regions
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "The statewide product against the aerial detection survey in four regions. Dead cells lay inside a spruce beetle polygon on white spruce of 2016 to 2024; living cells were forest the surveyors flew over, never inside a spruce beetle polygon of any year, within 10 km of one. AUC is the area under the curve for ranking dead above living; the two shares are the cells of each class the strip's VV threshold called susceptible; rho is Spearman's correlation between the year a dead cell was first recorded and its canopy height."
rt <- data.frame(Region = region_names[colnames(region_auc)], Dead = format(region_auc["dead", ], big.mark = ","), Living = format(region_auc["living", ], big.mark = ","),
  `AUC, VV` = sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", ]), `AUC, height` = sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_height", ]), `VV dead (dB)` = sprintf("%.1f", region_auc["VV_dead", ]), `VV living (dB)` = sprintf("%.1f", region_auc["VV_living", ]),
  `Susceptible, dead (%)` = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * region_auc["above_dead", ]), `Susceptible, living (%)` = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * region_auc["above_living", ]), `rho year, height` = ifelse(is.na(region_auc["rho_year_height", ]), "", sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["rho_year_height", ])), check.names = FALSE)
fmt_tbl(rt)
```

## Ground plots

On the ground the trees that died were the large ones. In the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, on the `r fia_ground["both", "matsu"]` plots holding both live and dead white spruce, the dead trees averaged `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["dia_dead", "matsu"])` cm in diameter and `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["ht_dead", "matsu"])` m in height against `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["dia_live", "matsu"])` cm and `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["ht_live", "matsu"])` m for the live trees [paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, V = `r format(fia_ground["V_dia", "matsu"], big.mark = ",")`, `r pfmt(fia_ground["p_dia", "matsu"])` for diameter and V = `r format(fia_ground["V_ht", "matsu"], big.mark = ",")`, `r pfmt(fia_ground["p_ht", "matsu"])` for height], and across the `r fia_ground["plots", "matsu"]` plots the share of white spruce basal area standing dead rose with the height of the tallest tree [Spearman's rho `r sprintf("%.2f", fia_ground["rho_share_ht", "matsu"])`], which ranked the `r fia_ground["half_dead", "matsu"]` plots with at least half their basal area dead with an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", fia_ground["AUC_ht_half", "matsu"])`. On the Kenai Peninsula the dead trees on the `r fia_ground["both", "kenai"]` plots holding both were again the larger, `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["dia_dead", "kenai"])` cm and `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["ht_dead", "kenai"])` m against `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["dia_live", "kenai"])` cm and `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["ht_live", "kenai"])` m [V = `r format(fia_ground["V_dia", "kenai"], big.mark = ",")`, `r pfmt(fia_ground["p_dia", "kenai"])` and V = `r format(fia_ground["V_ht", "kenai"], big.mark = ",")`, `r pfmt(fia_ground["p_ht", "kenai"])`]. In the Copper River basin the dead trees were `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["dia_dead", "copper"])` cm against `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["dia_live", "copper"])` cm on `r fia_ground["both", "copper"]` plots [V = `r format(fia_ground["V_dia", "copper"], big.mark = ",")`, `r pfmt(fia_ground["p_dia", "copper"])`], with no difference in height [V = `r format(fia_ground["V_ht", "copper"], big.mark = ",")`, `r pfmt(fia_ground["p_ht", "copper"])`]. On the Interior plots the dead white spruce on `r fia_ground["both", "interior"]` plots holding both were no thicker than the live ones, `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["dia_dead", "interior"])` against `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["dia_live", "interior"])` cm [V = `r format(fia_ground["V_dia", "interior"], big.mark = ",")`, `r pfmt(fia_ground["p_dia", "interior"])`], and were shorter, `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["ht_dead", "interior"])` against `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["ht_live", "interior"])` m [V = `r format(fia_ground["V_ht", "interior"], big.mark = ",")`, `r pfmt(fia_ground["p_ht", "interior"])`]. The satellite height around a plot's published coordinate ranked the half-dead plots at `r sprintf("%.2f", fia_remote["eth.AUC_half", "matsu"])` in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, against `r sprintf("%.2f", fia_ground["AUC_ht_half", "matsu"])` for the plot's own tallest tree.

# Discussion

Over the Susitna valley strip of @Zwieback_2024, the Sentinel-1 VV level of October 2014 to December 2016 ranked the stands that the outbreak would kill above the stands it left alive, with an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", change$auc_pre[change$band == "VV131"])` on the crown labels and `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["AUC"])` for the pooled statewide product on the severity map, while the change in the same cells through the outbreak ranked nothing. The first objective therefore has the answer that the radar is validated against the best ground truth that exists for this outbreak, and that what it validated is not a detection of mortality but a measurement of the stand before it. Three canopy heights measured by different physics, lidar fitted to optical imagery, X-band radar stereo and optical stereo, ranked the same cells about as well as the C-band level did, the dead cells stood `r sprintf("%.1f", struct["dead", "height_eth"] - struct["alive", "height_eth"])` m taller on the ETH map, and the product's rank correlation with height over the forest was `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["rho_height"])`, so the radar level measured stand height and the map is a map of tall stands.

That the tall stands died is the oldest finding in the spruce beetle literature, and the review set out how firmly it stands. @Massey_1954 [p. 13] found that the beetle "prefers the large, more mature trees", @Werner_1983 [p. 96] that "Mortality was greatest in the larger diameter classes during the early part of the infestation", @Hard_1985b [p. 7] that "Spruce beetles preferentially attack and kill large diameter trees that have been growing slowly at breast height", and @Doak_2004 [p. 810] that "Mortality increased with increasing DBH and decreasing BAI". The present study found the same rule at the scale of the stand, from free satellite data, with no beetle in the predictor, and the inventory plots confirmed it on the ground in the same decade, the dead white spruce standing `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["dia_dead", "matsu"] - fia_ground["dia_live", "matsu"])` cm thicker and `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["ht_dead", "matsu"] - fia_ground["ht_live", "matsu"])` m taller than the live trees beside them in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough and `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["dia_dead", "kenai"] - fia_ground["dia_live", "kenai"])` cm thicker on the Kenai Peninsula. The Interior plots, measured in `r fia_ground["from", "interior"]` to `r fia_ground["to", "interior"]` before the outbreak's front entered the Denali Borough, gave the comparison the design needed, in that where the beetle had not yet been the dead white spruce were no thicker and `r sprintf("%.1f", fia_ground["ht_live", "interior"] - fia_ground["ht_dead", "interior"])` m shorter than the live, as ordinary mortality takes the suppressed trees, so the size effect belongs to the beetle and not to death in general. The order of attack held as well. The stands the survey recorded first in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, in 2016 and 2017, were the tallest and the height of each year's new stands fell through to 2024, as @Massey_1954 recorded in the White River outbreak and @Werner_1983 on the Kenai, where the beetle took the large trees first and moved to smaller ones as the outbreak proceeded. The contrast held inside each LANDFIRE class with enough cells, including the one white spruce class, so it was a contrast between tall and short stands of the same cover and not between host and non-host.

The second objective was met in two regions of three, under the ceiling that the survey sets. Against the aerial detection survey the radar map ranked attacked above unattacked forest at `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", "kenai"])` on the Kenai Peninsula and `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", "matsu"])` in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, and every one of nine sources, three heights, two L-band mosaics and the single-orbit radar levels, scored between `r sprintf("%.2f", min(matsu["AUC", ]))` and `r sprintf("%.2f", max(matsu["AUC", ]))` against the same label in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, where the crown map had scored them at `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["AUC", "VV65_pre"])` to `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["AUC", "height_eth"])`. The survey is sketched from an aircraft at a scale at which a polygon of 2 per cent mortality is mostly living forest, and restricting the dead cells to polygons of 20 per cent mortality or more changed nothing, so the ceiling is the label's and not the map's. The regional numbers are therefore a lower bound on the map's skill, and the strip numbers its measure where the label is good. In the Copper River basin the radar level failed where the height map did not, `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", "copper"])` against `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_height", "copper"])`, and the two means say why the two measures parted. The attacked stands there were `r sprintf("%.1f", region_auc["height_dead", "copper"])` m tall against `r sprintf("%.1f", region_auc["height_dead", "matsu"])` m in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough and the radar level of both classes sat near `r sprintf("%.0f", region_auc["VV_living", "copper"])` dB, so the open spruce woodland of the basin lies below the range in which the C-band level follows height, and there the level is set by the ground and not by the canopy. The radar product is therefore validated for the Kenai Peninsula and the Susitna lowlands, where the strip and the two regions agree, and the height map carries the Copper River basin, which is the shrinking of the extent that the design allowed for. The area the map calls susceptible in the Valdez-Cordova census area (@tbl-area) is not a contradiction of that failure, because the census area runs to the coast and the tall Sitka spruce forest of Prince William Sound lies above the threshold while the basin's woodland lies below it. In the Interior the map scored `r sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", "interior"])` against the survey at the front of the outbreak along the Nenana River, where most of the recorded cells date from 2021 or later, which is the number a front in its first years should give, because the polygons there hold stands the beetle has entered and not yet killed through, and the inventory plots of the same region, measured before the front arrived, showed no size effect at all.

The hazard ratings of @Schmid_1976, @Reynolds_1994b and @Fettig_2026 need basal area, spruce share and mean diameter from a cruise, and the Forest Service has never been able to rate the forest of a state. The map gives a rating of the same kind at 90 m across `r format(round(state_area$forest_km2[state_area$region == "alaska"]), big.mark = ",")` km² of forest from free data, with `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * state_area$susceptible_km2[state_area$region == "alaska"] / state_area$forest_km2[state_area$region == "alaska"])` per cent of that forest at or above the level at which the strip's stands died, and it carries the attributes the ratings carry, height standing for the large dominant spruce and the radar level for height and biomass together (@tbl-attributes). The limits are those of the sources and the label. The ETH height is a 2020 model, contemporary with the outbreak in the Susitna valley, while the GLO-30 and ArcticDEM surfaces, the 2007 to 2010 PALSAR mosaic and the 2014 to 2016 radar predate it and gave the same ranking. The pooling of orbits rests on one fitted fall of backscatter with incidence angle, `r sprintf("%.3f", angle_slope)` dB per degree, and on a median scene count behind a forest cell that ran from `r min(state_area$scenes)` in the thinnest region to `r max(state_area$scenes)` in the densest. The map says nothing about spruce share, so a tall birch or aspen stand scores as a tall spruce stand would, and a manager reads it with the stand map in hand. The threshold was set on one valley, and a region whose stands are taller or shorter than the Susitna valley's will have more or fewer cells above it than the beetle will take.

# Conclusion

The pre-outbreak Sentinel-1 radar level and three independent canopy heights ranked the stands the spruce beetle killed in the Susitna valley above the stands it left alive, against the crown labels and severity map of @Zwieback_2024, with an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["AUC", "height_eth"])` to `r sprintf("%.2f", change$auc_pre[change$band == "VV131"])`, and the stands that died stood `r sprintf("%.1f", struct["dead", "height_eth"] - struct["alive", "height_eth"])` m taller before the outbreak reached them. The finding is the one the Alaska and Rocky Mountain plot studies have reported since 1954, that the beetle takes the large mature spruce first, found here at the scale of the stand from free satellite data with no beetle in the predictor. Pooled across every scene over Alaska, the level gave a 90 m map of susceptible stands across `r format(round(state_area$forest_km2[state_area$region == "alaska"]), big.mark = ",")` km² of forest, which ranked attacked above unattacked forest on the Kenai Peninsula and in the Susitna lowlands but not in the open woodland of the Copper River basin, where the height map held, and which the inventory plots confirmed on the ground, and the two maps are offered to the managers preparing their stands for the next outbreak.

## Data availability

All inputs were publicly available and were read by the code shown in this manuscript, except the severity map of Zwieback (2023), which carries no declared licence and was used for validation only. The crown labels of @Zwieback_2024 were downloaded from Zenodo under the licence given in the code; the Sentinel-1 scenes, the Copernicus 30 m digital elevation model, the ETH canopy height, the USGS 3D Elevation Program terrain, the ArcticDEM mosaic, the PALSAR mosaics, the LANDFIRE vegetation type and the census boundaries were read in Google Earth Engine under the asset names given in the code; the aerial detection survey damage and surveyed areas and the Forest Inventory and Analysis tables were downloaded from the United States Forest Service, and the conifer top cover from the Oak Ridge National Laboratory Distributed Active Archive Center. The 90 m statewide map is held as the Earth Engine asset named in the code. The sampled backscatter of each cell, the regional samples, the screening table of the literature review and the tables and figures are held with the manuscript under `02.inputs/derived`, `04.references/review` and `03.outputs`, and every number in the text is computed from them at render time.
